Job Details:

General Notes

The McDonald Observatory is a major astronomical research facility in the Davis Mountains of West Texas, in Fort Davis, Texas (440 miles from the UT Austin campus). The Observatory offers state-of-the-art telescopes and research instruments, hosts global observatories, and engages the public through educational programs.

This position is based on the UT Austin campus and coordinates travel and official occasion entertainment requests and payments for McDonald Observatory and the Department of Astronomy. Responsibilities include travel arrangements and reimbursement, assistance with official occasion requests, and accounts payable and receivable processing. This position helps ensure policy compliance and consistent coverage

UT Austin offers a competitive benefits package that includes:

  • 100% employer-paid basic medical coverage.  

  • Retirement contributions: Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS)

  • Paid vacation and sick time. 

  • Paid holidays. 

  • Please visit our Human Resources (HR) website to learn more about the total benefits offered.

Purpose

The Travel and Entertainment Specialist serves as the primary point of contact and resource for departmental business travel and entertainment requests and payments. In this role, you assist with and arrange travel for staff, faculty, students, and non-employees, and process reimbursements. Process entertainment documentation and expenses in coordination with the business officer for official occasions. As a business office team member, you support administrative and departmental operations and accounts receivable, accounts payable, and purchasing as required.

Responsibilities

  • Travel Request and Processing. Receive and process travel authorizations (RTA) from faculty, staff, students, and visitors, and arrange travel or confirm self-arrangements, requesting additional documentation as needed. Before processing, obtain the necessary approvals from supervisors and account holders, and ensure compliance with UT and departmental policies. Verify account compliance and funding. Research and make reservations by phone, online, or through a travel agent for airfare, car rentals, registrations, etc. Secure lodging and include traveler information if requested. Communicate effectively with travelers and troubleshoot issues, offering possible resolutions.

  • Travel Reimbursement and Vendor Payments. Prepare and promptly process accurate travel reimbursement vouchers for department faculty, staff, students, and visitors, ensuring compliance with UT and departmental policies. Process vendor payments billed directly to the department. Provide documentation and support for contract payments and for departmental Citibank ProCard and Travel Card transactions. Prepare interdepartmental transfer vouchers to charge food, lodging, and car rentals to the appropriate accounts. Monitor travel budgets to ensure compliance with account requirements, and process account transfers and charge corrections as directed. Maintain accurate documentation for all transactions. Prepare reports, such as expenses by department code or allocation.

  • Entertainment and Official Occasion Process and Reimbursement. Reviews requests for entertainment for business purposes, confirms fund sources that may be used for such purposes, and provides guidance for the reasonable expenditure of funds or other expenses often related to reimbursement from institutional funds. Ensures compliance with department procedures, state laws, IRS, and UT System Regents rules.

  • Business Office Support. Communicate and collaborate with the business office team and stakeholders. Perform and back up coworkers’ administrative, purchasing, and accounts payable duties as required, and provide ongoing team support to meet business needs.

  • Compliance and Reporting. Maintains travel and entertainment policies and ensures compliance with department, campus, state, and federal guidelines. Liaise with Travel Management Services and stay current on the university's travel policies and procedures. Assist faculty, staff, students, and researchers in interpreting and implementing these policies. Communicate and post website updates as procedures change. Identify process and resource efficiencies to meet customer needs.

Required Qualifications

  • High school graduation or GED.

  • Experience with Microsoft Office suite, including an intermediate skill level in Excel and Word.

  • Working knowledge of travel and entertainment policy, expense reimbursement rules, or the ability to learn them quickly.

  • Ability to assess high-volume workload and prioritize tasks while demonstrating attention to detail and accuracy to meet deadlines and manage concurrent projects in multiple areas successfully.

  • Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, including customer-service excellence for handling inquiries from the department.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, with strong writing and proofreading skills.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

  • Ability to interact and maintain productive working relationships with staff, faculty, students, and visitors, and maintain a positive and professional demeanor.

  • Ability to learn quickly and be flexible.

  • Experience taking ownership of projects and seeing them through to successful completion.

  • Ability to undertake and complete tasks with minimal supervision and exhibit individual initiative in meeting the functions of the position.

  • Professional demeanor and dependability.

  • Ability to exercise a high level of discretion and handle sensitive or confidential matters with professionalism and care.

  • Reliable and dependable attendance.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field.

  • Strong knowledge and experience in travel and entertainment expense review, audit, approval, compliance, or reimbursement documents in a high-volume environment, preferably in higher education.

  • Experience using UT mainframe, UT request system, and other UT applications.

  • Knowledge of the UT travel policies and procedures, including Concur travel and expense management.

  • Experience planning travel and working with Travel Management.

  • Advanced skills in the use of Microsoft Office applications and Smartsheet.

  • Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new systems, adapt to change, and work collaboratively.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Salary Range

$50,000 + depending on qualifications and experience

Working Conditions

  • Work at a computer and in standard office conditions with repetitive keyboard use at a workstation.

  • Use of manual dexterity.

  • Lifting and moving.

  • Additional hours may be required during peak and after-hours for travel assistance.

Work Shift

  • Standard business hours, Monday - Friday

  • May need to work occasional after-hours or weekends

Required Materials

  • Letter of Interest

  • Resume/CV

  • Three work references with their contact information; at least one reference should be from a supervisor

Application Instructions

  • Applicants who are NOT current university employees or contingent workers: You will be prompted to submit your resume the first time you apply. You will be allowed to upload a new Resume for subsequent applications. Any additional Required Materials (letter of interest, references, etc.) will be uploaded in the Application Questions section; you can multi-select additional files. Before submitting your online job application, ensure that ALL Required Materials have been uploaded. Once your job application has been submitted, you cannot make changes.

  • Current university employees and contingent workers: As a current university employee or contingent worker, you MUST apply within Workday by searching for Find UT Jobs. If you are a current University employee, log in to Workday, navigate to your Worker Profile, click the Career link in the left-hand navigation menu, and then update the sections in your Professional Profile before you apply. This information will be pulled into your application. The application is one page, and you will be prompted to upload your resume. title: Business Analyst (12 Month MTC)
description:
Challenger Limited is an ASX-listed investment management firm managing $128 billion in assets (as at 31 March 2026). Life with us is fast moving and always exciting. Together we’re driving to deliver our vision to provide our customers with financial security for a better retirement.

We achieve this goal by providing a work environment where people from diverse backgrounds, with a range of skills and experiences can contribute and succeed.


Business Analyst – Customer Program Management – 12 Month MTC

  • Join Challenger as a Business Analyst and play a key role in delivering initiatives that improve customer outcomes and support business growth.

  • Enjoy variety, with the opportunity to work across regulatory, technology, operational and customer-focused projects.

  • Partner with stakeholders across the business, influencing decisions and helping turn complex requirements into practical solutions.

  • At Challenger, we work flexibly. You can expect to spend three days each week in our Sydney CBD office and two days working from home.

About the role

As a Business Analyst in our Customer Program Management team, you'll work across projects spanning large-scale transitions, technology delivery, customer initiatives and strategic partnerships.

Partnering with stakeholders across the business, you'll help shape solutions by exploring, challenging and translating business needs into clear functional and technical outcomes. You'll facilitate discussions, test assumptions and work with stakeholders to uncover the requirements needed to support successful delivery.

You'll work closely with business stakeholders, technology teams and delivery partners, providing the business context, requirements and decision support needed to move initiatives successfully from discovery through to delivery.

As part of an integrated programme team, you'll work alongside Project Managers, Release Managers, Change Managers and delivery partners to help ensure requirements remain aligned throughout the delivery lifecycle and are translated into meaningful business outcomes.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Facilitating workshops to uncover business needs, challenge assumptions, align stakeholders and drive decisions.

  • Eliciting, documenting and analysing business, functional and technical requirements.

  • Conducting impact assessments and validating requirements to ensure proposed solutions meet business needs.

  • Working closely with delivery partners, providing business context, acceptance criteria and ongoing support throughout delivery.

  • Using data and gap analysis to test assumptions, identify insights and inform solution design.

  • Mapping current and future-state processes to improve customer outcomes, efficiency and controls.

  • Producing and maintaining key project artefacts, including requirements documentation and process maps.

What we're looking for

You'll bring proven Business Analyst experience within a corporate financial services environment, with strong capability in requirements elicitation, process analysis and stakeholder engagement.

Experience working as a business analyst within financial services is essential, with experience in insurance or, superannuation environments highly regarded. Exposure to technology-enabled transformation programmes will also be highly regarded.

You're naturally curious and enjoy understanding how things work. You're comfortable asking questions, challenging assumptions and helping stakeholders work through complex problems to reach practical outcomes.

You can navigate complexity, balance detail with the bigger picture and communicate confidently with a broad range of stakeholders, including customers, partners and senior leaders.

You’ll also bring:

  • Strong workshop facilitation and stakeholder management skills.

  • Experience translating business needs into clear functional and technical requirements.

  • Strong process mapping, impact assessment and requirements validation capability.

  • Proficiency in business analysis tools, techniques and methodologies.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.

  • Experience with JIRA, Confluence and MS Project.

  • Familiarity with governance, risk and regulatory frameworks.

Why Challenger

You'll be part of a collaborative, people-focused environment where different perspectives are valued and employees are encouraged to contribute, build their capability and make an impact.

Working across a diverse portfolio of business, technology and customer initiatives, you'll have the opportunity to help shape solutions from early discovery through to delivery and adoption, partnering with teams across Challenger and our delivery partner network.

Challenger also provides flexible working and a range of benefits supporting wellbeing, family life, career development and financial wellbeing.

At Challenger, we provide access to a range of exclusive employee benefits that will support you both personally and professionally and a hybrid work environment. Visit our benefits page for more information.

https://www.challenger.com.au/about-us/careers/our-benefits

#LI-Challenger #LI-KM1 #LI-Hybrid

Challenger's employee value proposition guides how we work: Grow and realise your potential, supporting each other, stronger together and making things happen. Our culture encourages curiosity, considered thinking and meaningful contribution, with opportunities to build a broad and rewarding career.

We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace where people of all backgrounds, identities and ways of thinking can thrive, and promoting flexible working to support work-life balance.

title: Operations & Service Management Lead
description:

Lead technology operations, service management and continual improvement within a leading research and investment organisation.

title: Shift Planner
description:
Shift Planner

CLS Production Planning

Job Description

Introduction

ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our main headquarters is located in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we also have 18 office locations around the United States- including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.

As a Shift Planner at ASML, you will help keep our manufacturing operations running smoothly. Your work ensures that critical materials move efficiently into, through, and out of the cleanroom. In this role, you will collaborate across Production Logistics, Production Planning, Material Handling, and Manufacturing to maintain flow and remove obstacles that could slow down progress. The Shift Planner is key to keeping our factory teams productive and aligned.

Role and Responsibilities

As a Shift Planner, you coordinate daily production activities and ensure materials arrive where and when they are needed. You monitor work in progress, maintain communication with planning and logistics teams, and help solve issues that could delay production. You also support improvement initiatives and help keep inventory data accurate. In this role, you contribute directly to operational stability and build readiness.

  • Support daily execution of the production plan in consultation with Production Planning.

  • Monitor work orders in progress and confirm that logistics needs are met on time.

  • Manage expedited movement of materials from the warehouse to the cleanroom.

  • Review completed work orders to validate material usage.

  • Join daily meetings to review the build plan and address risks.

  • Troubleshoot logistics issues that could disrupt manufacturing and share prevention ideas.

  • Communicate production concerns and escalate critical blocks when needed.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, logistics, industrial engineering, business, or a related field; or equivalent years of relevant work experience.

  • Minimum of two years of relevant business experience required. Experience in a complex or high‑volume production environment preferred.

  • Understanding of planning and production concepts such as material requirements planning, just‑in‑time, and lean principles preferred.

  • Experience using enterprise resource planning systems such as ORACLE a plus.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Excel, and PowerPoint.

Skills

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:

  • Communicate clearly and professionally across teams.

  • Collaborate with colleagues and contribute to team goals.

  • Stay organized and manage tasks in a fast‑paced environment.

  • Act proactively to prevent delays or errors.

  • Analyze issues and recommend practical solutions.

  • Take ownership of assigned tasks and follow them to completion.

  • Adapt quickly to new information or changes in priorities.

  • Solve problems creatively and with persistence.

  • Provide helpful, service‑oriented support to factory teams.

  • Maintain focus while working with cutting‑edge technology.

Other Information

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • The environment is primarily within a cleanroom, moderate in temperature and noise level.

  • The employee is required to move around the campus, including the loading dock.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to sit, stand, walk, talk, hear, and use hands to keyboard.

  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

  • The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.

  • This position is located on-site in San Diego, CA. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation.

  • The position may require travel depending on business needs.

You must be work authorized in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship.

The current base annual hourly range for this role is currently:

$31-42

Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members.

The Company offers employees and their families, medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. Employees will also receive eight (8) hours of vacation leave every month and (13) paid holidays throughout the calendar year. title: Founding AI Engineer
description:
Jetty is building the first AI functional health doctor & coach. We're starting with solutions for people living with chronic illness, the hardest use case. Our mission is to help people become their own best advocates by giving them an intelligent partner that evolves with their health journey, helping them understand what their body is telling them.
Health data is uniquely hard: personal, messy, and constantly changing. Symptoms ebb and flow rather than turning on and off. Patterns emerge over weeks, not sessions. And the signals that matter—what actually helps someone feel better—are different for everyone.
We're building infrastructure to capture and reason about this data in ways that compound over time: rich data modeling, precise timeline handling, and personalization that improves with every interaction. Our approach treats models not as chat interfaces but as components in larger systems—generating artifacts, managing state, and themselves accumulating the signal needed to train specialized models.
We’re a small, high-velocity team with big ambition. We move fast, think deeply, and care about substance over hype. If you want to build the definitive personal health intelligence from day one, this is the place. This is our first engineering hire, so you'll work directly with the founding team: a former senior AI leader from Palantir and a former venture investor from NEA.
Jetty is backed by the top seed investor in NYC and recently raised over $2M.
The Role
We're looking for a Founding AI Engineer to build the core systems that make Jetty intelligent — and that make it stay intelligent over months of use.
Most LLM products are stateless: every conversation starts from scratch. Jetty is different. We're building infrastructure where every interaction feeds forward — data flows into context, context shapes insight, insight drives value, and value brings people back. Your job is to build the systems that make this loop work: the data pipelines, memory architecture, and context layers that let Jetty surface genuinely novel insights even after months of use.
This sits at the intersection of backend engineering and AI-native product development. You'll own API design, database schema, and infrastructure — but the interesting part is figuring out how to make a probabilistic model behave like a reliable, evolving health partner.
You’ll be joining a live product with active users, not a blank repo. We have a solid foundation, but the architecture for deep, long-term health intelligence is still being defined—and you’ll help write it.
This is a remote or hybrid role (preference for US time zones), with optional in-person time in NYC for collaboration.
What You'll Do
  • Product Development: Build core features that make Jetty a faster, smarter, and more delightful product.
  • LLM Engineering: Design systems where models are components in larger workflows — not just chat endpoints, but nodes that generate, validate, and compose structured outputs. You'll shape context architecture, memory systems, and the configurations that let intelligence flow through the product.
  • Infrastructure & Reliability: Work around the full lifecycle of code — CI/CD, deployments, observability. Build systems that scale gracefully and fail safely.
  • Work with Hard Data: Health data is sparse, vague, and temporal. You'll build systems that extract signal from conversational inputs without imposing false precision.
  • Build & Iterate: We invest in foundations where they compound, and move fast on everything else. You'll do both.

What We're Looking For
  • 3–6+ years experience as a software engineer.
  • Strong in Python
  • Instincts for reliability, scaling, security, and observability.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and early-stage chaos. You should be comfortable with rapid iteration and high expectations for both speed and quality. As a result, you’ll be able to own meaningful projects end-to-end.
  • Experience with (or genuine excitement for) creative LLM engineering—not just calling endpoints, but shaping model behavior through context design and system architecture.
  • Bonus:
    • Swift, frontend skills, or experience with real-time systems.
    • Experience with strongly typed or compiled languages (Go, Rust, Java, etc.)
    • Experience with real-time systems

What We Offer
  • The opportunity to build a product that genuinely changes how people manage their health.
  • Competitive salary & meaningful equity package.
  • Real ownership and impact from day one.

title: Sr. Director, Business Systems Analysis
description:
Description

Senior Director, Pharmacy Management System & Automation (RPA)

Reports to: VP, Analytics & Optimization | Function: Operational Excellence & Automation

Role Summary

The Senior Director, Pharmacy Management System & Automation will own the Pharmacy Management System (PMS), automation strategy (RPA), and process improvement capability across Specialty Pharmacy Services and 340B operations.

This leader will serve as the critical bridge between pharmacy operations, process improvement, and technology — bringing dedicated ownership and governance to capabilities currently distributed across multiple teams. The role will enable the business to scale to 175+ pharmacies by optimizing processes, reducing variation, and leveraging technology and automation to increase operational capacity without proportional increases in labor.

Key Responsibilities

Pharmacy Management System

  • Own the PMS as a business capability, including business requirements, configuration, workflow design, optimization, governance, and roadmap priorities, in partnership with the Technology organization that owns and supports the platform.
  • Translate pharmacy and 340B operational needs into clear system requirements and scalable solutions.
  • Drive standardization and optimization of PMS workflows across pharmacy locations to improve efficiency, quality, consistency, and the end-user experience.

Automation & RPA

  • Develop and execute the automation/RPA strategy across Specialty Pharmacy and 340B operations, identifying and prioritizing high-value opportunities to eliminate repetitive and non-value-added manual work.
  • Deploy automation across key operational use cases, including 340B qualification rule configuration, audit processing and reconciliation, and other high-volume transactional workflows.
  • Build repeatable automation solutions that reduce manual touchpoints and errors, improve productivity, and create additional operational capacity.

Process Improvement & Scale

  • Lead Lean Six Sigma (LSS) and continuous process improvement efforts across the operation, identifying root causes of inefficiency and reducing unnecessary process variation.
  • Evaluate end-to-end workflows to identify opportunities for simplification, standardization, automation, and improved system utilization.
  • Build system- and automation-driven processes that enable the pharmacy footprint to scale to 175+ locations while maintaining quality, consistency, and service.
  • Partner closely with Pharmacy Operations, 340B, Analytics, Product, Technology, and other business leaders to align system, automation, and process improvement priorities with business needs and measurable outcomes.

What Success Looks Like (first 12–24 months)

  • Clear ownership and governance established for PMS optimization, automation, and process improvement across SPS and 340B.
  • High-value automation opportunities prioritized and deployed, including key 340B and pharmacy operational workflows.
  • Manual and non-value-added work measurably reduced, improving productivity and allowing pharmacy teams to focus more time on higher-value activities and customer service.
  • Standardized workflows and reduced process variation driving greater quality, consistency, and efficiency across the operation.
  • Increased operational capacity supporting growth to 175+ pharmacies without proportional increases in headcount.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmacy technology, pharmacy operations, automation, process improvement, or related functions, including significant leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated expertise with pharmacy management systems and a strong understanding of pharmacy and/or 340B operational workflows.
  • Deep experience with RPA, workflow automation, Lean Six Sigma/process improvement, and operational optimization in complex, high-volume environments.
  • Strong ability to bridge technology and operations — understands both system capabilities and real-world business processes and can translate effectively between the two.
  • Demonstrated experience identifying root causes, reducing process variation, and implementing technology-enabled solutions that deliver measurable productivity, quality, and scalability improvements.
  • Pharmacy and/or 340B experience strongly preferred, including familiarity with 340B qualification rules, audit processes, and operational workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience leading significant transformation and change initiatives across multiple functions.

Competencies

  • Technology + operations translator — connects system capabilities with real-world pharmacy and 340B operational needs.
  • Automation-first mindset — looks for opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate before adding manual processes or incremental resources.
  • Continuous improvement leader — uses data and disciplined problem-solving to address root causes and eliminate process variation.
  • End-user focused — improves the experience of pharmacy teams by reducing unnecessary manual work and designing intuitive, effective workflows.
  • Scales by design — builds systems, processes, and automation capable of supporting significant growth without proportional increases in complexity or labor.

title: Service Director Ford & CDJR
description:
Automotive Service Director – Ford & CDJR

Veero Ford & Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram | Morris, Minnesota

Job Type: Full-Time

Schedule: Monday–Friday, with occasional Saturday coverage as needed

Work Location: On-site in Morris, Minnesota

About Veero Ford & CDJR

At Veero Ford & Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram, we believe great service starts with great people. Our dealership is built on small-town values, accountability, and treating customers like neighbors rather than numbers.

We are committed to developing our employees, investing in training, and building a service department that delivers exceptional customer experiences and strong operational performance.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to take ownership of a dual-franchise service department, make a meaningful impact, and help shape its future.

Life in Morris, Minnesota

Enjoy the charm of small-town living with affordable housing, short commutes, friendly neighbors, and easy access to beautiful lakes and outdoor recreation.

Morris offers a welcoming community where you can build a rewarding career while enjoying a great quality of life for you and your family.

Position Overview

Veero Ford & CDJR is seeking an experienced, hands-on Automotive Service Director to lead our dual-franchise Ford and Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram service department.

We are looking for a proven dealership service leader who understands how to manage technicians, develop service advisors, improve shop productivity, and deliver exceptional customer experiences while maintaining strong departmental profitability.

The Service Director will work closely with ownership to strengthen daily operations, develop employees, improve processes, and build a department positioned for long-term success.

This is an opportunity for a leader who wants to take ownership of a department, implement meaningful improvements, and build a high-performing team.

Key Responsibilities

Service Department Leadership

  • Oversee daily service operations, including technicians, service advisors, dispatching, and shop workflow.

  • Lead, coach, and develop service advisors, technicians, and support staff.

  • Establish clear performance expectations and maintain accountability.

  • Manage technician scheduling, shop capacity, and repair order flow.

  • Recruit, train, and retain qualified service personnel.

  • Foster a positive, professional, and customer-focused work environment.

Operational Performance & Productivity

  • Monitor and improve technician productivity, efficiency, and hours per repair order (HPRO).

  • Manage effective labor rate (ELR), customer-pay labor sales, and labor gross profit.

  • Improve repair order processes, multipoint inspection completion, and declined service follow-up.

  • Ensure accurate repair documentation, quality control, and timely completion of repairs.

  • Maintain compliance with Ford and Stellantis warranty policies and procedures.

  • Identify opportunities to improve shop capacity, workflow, and overall department performance.

Financial Management

  • Take responsibility for service department sales, gross profit, and controllable expenses.

  • Establish and monitor departmental performance goals and key performance indicators.

  • Review financial results and identify opportunities to improve profitability.

  • Manage labor pricing, technician productivity, and service sales performance.

Customer Experience

  • Maintain high standards for customer satisfaction and service retention.

  • Resolve escalated customer concerns professionally and promptly.

  • Monitor customer satisfaction surveys, online reviews, and service follow-up.

  • Ensure service advisors communicate clearly with customers regarding repair recommendations, estimates, and completion times.

  • Build lasting customer relationships and strengthen the dealership's reputation in the community.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Minimum 2 years of dealership service management or assistant service management experience.

  • Proven ability to lead technicians and service advisors.

  • Strong understanding of dealership service operations, workflow, and financial performance.

  • Experience managing technician productivity, effective labor rate, and departmental profitability.

  • Strong communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently, make decisions, and maintain accountability.

Preferred:

  • Previous Ford or Stellantis dealership experience.

  • Experience managing a dual-franchise service department.

  • Familiarity with Ford and Stellantis warranty procedures and manufacturer requirements.

  • Experience improving service department profitability and customer satisfaction.

  • Experience recruiting and developing automotive technicians.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation: $87k- 120k per year, including potential performance-based bonuses.

Starting base salary is determined by relevant dealership management experience, qualifications, manufacturer experience, and demonstrated operational results.

Additional earnings are available through a performance-based bonus plan tied to service department profitability and productivity.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance.

  • 401(k) with company match.

  • Paid time off and holidays.

  • Paid manufacturer training and professional development.

  • Life insurance.

  • Health Savings Account (HSA) availability.

  • Employee vehicle purchase discounts.

  • Relocation assistance for qualified candidates.

  • Long-term career development opportunities.

Tuition-Free College Education for You and Your Family

Through our Degrees@Work program, employees and eligible family members may have access to tuition-free college education opportunities.

Whether you're looking to earn a degree, advance your career, or help a family member pursue higher education, this benefit can provide valuable educational opportunities.

Ask us for details about available programs, participating schools, and eligibility requirements.

Why Join Veero Ford & CDJR?

This is an opportunity for an experienced service leader who wants more than simply managing the day-to-day operation.

You will have the opportunity to build a strong team, improve processes, develop technicians, and take ownership of a service department representing two major automotive manufacturers.

Our dealership offers direct access to ownership, the opportunity to implement your ideas, and the ability to make a measurable impact on the business.

If you are a hands-on leader who takes pride in developing people, improving performance, and delivering exceptional customer service, we would like to hear from you.

Candidates from Minnesota and across the United States are encouraged to apply. This position is located in Morris, Minnesota, and relocation assistance is available for qualified candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Veero Ford & Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable law.

description:
Third Key Holder - Lawrenceville (1250 Scenic Hwy, Lawrenceville, GA 30045)

Hollywood Feed was established in the 1950s, in Memphis, TN, as a pet supply store with friendly and knowledgeable service. More than half a century later, our love for pets is who we are today. Our associates are family and the face of each location. We care about each other, our pets, and our customers. Come and experience the passion and drive that makes Hollywood Feed what it is today.

The Third Key Holder, who reports to the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, opens and closes the store, serves customers, and ensures safe, efficient, and profitable operations while upholding Hollywood Feed's first policy: "Do what is right by the customer."

title: Software Development Engineer III
description:
At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.


Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere.

Our Technology Team partners with teams across Expedia Group to create innovative products, services, and tools to deliver high-quality experiences for travelers, partners, and our employees. A singular technology platform powered by data and machine learning provides secure, differentiated, and personalized experiences that drive loyalty and traveler satisfaction.

Introduction to the Team

Expedia Group is revolutionizing the way people search for and book travel. As part of Product & Technology, the Distribution and Supply Tech - Inventory team builds the platform that ingests, stores, and distributes lodging rates and availability data across all Expedia Group brands. Using cloud technologies and modern engineering practices, we power travel shopping and booking experiences on a global scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, test, and deliver reliable software solutions across services and domains, applying strong coding fundamentals, low-level design, API design, and data modeling practices.

  • Own technical execution for complex components and services, translating business and product needs into scalable, maintainable engineering outcomes.

  • Contribute to system design and architecture decisions, balancing performance, availability, security, and operational excellence in production environments.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues, improve service health through monitoring and automation, and drive continuous improvements in quality, resilience, and developer efficiency.

  • Collaborate effectively with engineers and cross-functional partners to deliver end-to-end solutions, sharing technical knowledge and contributing across multiple technology areas as needed.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated success building scalable, high-availability systems and driving operational excellence through observability, automation, and performance optimization.

  • Strong judgment using data and metrics to identify issues, prioritize improvements, and inform technical decisions.

  • Experience contributing across the full stack or multiple technical domains, adapting quickly to new technologies and business problem spaces.

  • Experience evaluating or implementing AI/ML-enabled capabilities in software products, and using AI-driven development tools or workflows to improve engineering outcomes.

  • Experience working effectively in decentralized or geographically distributed teams.

title: Technical Apparel Designer Senior
description:
Technical Apparel Designer Senior

About the Role:

Endless Summer Technologies, a manufacturing division of SCUBAPRO, a Johnson Outdoors company, is one the most respected and recognized brands in the global diving industry. The brand is trusted by recreational and professional divers for more than 60 years. We are seeking a Technical Apparel Designer who will lead the end to end creative design of performance apparel products with a focus on fashion-forward design while also ensuring products meet brand standards, regulatory requirements, functional performance requirements, and manufacturing feasibility. You will be required to partner on a cross-functional team to provide design vision and leadership and to provide input into the product development plan, product concept development, innovation strategy, and product launch. In collaboration with engineering, you must ensure that products are designed based on the brand strategy, design specifications and product plans to ensure product success.

Johnson Outdoors operates globally with 1,300 employees across 18 facilities and a portfolio of market-leading brands in fishing, watercraft, camping, and diving. Together, we create amazing outdoor experiences for adventurers around the world in more than 80 countries.

Help Shape the Future of Diving

What you will do:

Fashion Design & Creative Direction

  • Leads the creative design vision for performance apparel, ensuring products reflect brand identity, aesthetic direction, and consumer appeal while maintaining functional intent.
  • Applies strong fashion design principles, including silhouette, color, trend, and storytelling to create innovative, commercially compelling products.
  • Leads the design and cosmetic development of performance apparel from concept through production.

Concept Development

  • Partners cross‑functionally on innovation, product concepts, and launches to drive brand and commercial results.
  • Executes product development initiatives, and translates brand vision, consumer insights, and performance requirements into innovative apparel concepts that balance style and performance.

Technical Design Execution

  • Develops detailed technical and cosmetic design specifications, including materials, construction, fit, trims, colorways, and artwork placement to support design intent. Creates and maintains tech packs, CADs, sketches, BOMs, and size specifications to clearly communicate intent to manufacturers.

Costs and Production Planning

  • Estimates production costs, identifies cost saving methods, and makes design decisions with a clear understanding of their impact on manufacturing cost and required investments.

Competitiveness Analysis

  • Analyzes/researches competitor products, fashion trends, and leading practices to provide recommendations on new design direction, materials, finishing, assembly, size/weight and performance.

Vendor and External Partner Management

  • Manages relationships with external vendors and partners to ensure targets, timelines and quality are achieved. Provides direction to vendors in prototype manufacturing, runs vendor inspections to streamline production processes and maintain expenses.

Engineering and Product Quality

  • Partners closely with internal teams on technical processes and testing to ensure products align with design intent, specifications, timelines, and budgets while meeting quality/compliance requirements. Reviews prototypes, samples, pre-production units and provides test feedback.

Continuous Improvement

  • Uses consumer feedback and performance insights to improve designs, address technical issues, and enhance efficiency and market impact.

    What you need to succeed:

    • Bachelor’s degree in fashion design, apparel design, industrial design or equivalent.
    • Typically requires 5 years of experience designing performance apparel, preferably outdoor which includes leading end-to-end design and cosmetic development , developing detailed technical specifications and partnering cross-functionally to deliver high-quality, market-completive products.
    • Strong foundation in fashion design principles (silhouette, color, materials, and trend application) combined with an understanding of performance apparel design, construction methods, and fit.
    • Ability to translate consumer insights and market trends into commercially successful product designs, balancing aesthetics with functional requirements.
    • Hands‑on experience creating technical specifications and working directly with domestic and/or overseas manufacturing partners. Ability to balance fashion trends with technical performance and manufacturability.
    • Experience operating as an autonomous individual contributor with ownership for design decisions.
    • Proficiency in design and technical tools such as Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, PLM systems, and CAD software.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to collaborate effectively with diverse individuals and effectively present to multiple teams, and to clearly convey design intent and specifications to manufacturers.
    • Excellent cross‑functional collaboration skills with the ability to influence without direct authority.
    • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent product development projects on schedule, within budget, and to defined quality standards.
    • Detail‑oriented with a strong commitment to product quality and consistency.
    • Skills and proven success in executing product development plans and strategies to support the development of innovative and profitable products. Understanding of product margins/financials and significant analytical ability.

    A few pointers about our culture:

    • Entrepreneurial spirit and innovation are in our bones! We authentically innovate trusted equipment that gets people out in the great outdoors.
    • We are laser-focused on our consumers, and passionate about providing superior solutions flexible to meet any event’s needs or mission requirements.
    • We strive to create meaningful, healthy change in the world as individuals and as a family of brands.
    • We value team members who are willing to wear many hats; who take personal initiative, anticipating what needs to be done, and figuring things out to make them happen; but who are also willing to ask help, to assist others and work together.

    What you will receive:

    • Share in the company’s success with competitive base salary with additional earning potential through participation in the management bonus program, and eligibility for annual pay increases.
    • Find work/life balance
    • Further your career with performance development and training opportunities, including our tuition assistance program.
    • Have fun at work, enjoying a collaborative and casual work environment.

    Business & Brand Snapshot

    • Industry: Outdoor Recreation & Consumer Products
    • Business Unit: Diving
    • Brands: SCUBAPRO®
    • Products: Dive Computers, Regulators, BCDs, Dive Instruments, Underwater Equipment and Accessories
    • Key Skills: Global Trade Show Management, Retail Merchandising, POP/POS Display Development, Sales Enablement, Dealer Marketing, Brand Activation, Sales Enablement, Field Marketing Leadership, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Go-to-Market Strategy, Marketing Analytics, Event Marketing
    • Technology Focus: Dive Computers, Wearable Technology, Underwater Electronics, Pressure Systems, Life-Support Equipment, Connected Devices

    JOHNSON OUTDOORS is a leading global innovator of outdoor recreation equipment and technologies that inspire more people to experience the awe of the great outdoors. The company designs, manufactures and markets a portfolio of winning, consumer-preferred brands across four categories: Watercraft Recreation, Fishing, Diving and Camping. Johnson Outdoors' iconic brands include: Old Town® canoes and kayaks; Ocean Kayak™; Carlisle® paddles; Minn Kota® fishing motors, batteries and anchors; Cannon® downriggers; Humminbird® marine electronics and charts; SCUBAPRO® dive equipment; Jetboil® outdoor cooking systems. title: Software Systems Engineer, Lead
description:
Software Systems Engineer, Lead

Are you looking for an opportunity to combine your technical skills with big picture thinking to make an impact in Space Electronic Warfare? You understand your customer’s environment and how to develop the right systems for their mission. Your ability to translate real-world needs into technical specifications makes you an integral part of delivering a customer focused engineering solution.

As a leader in systems engineering, we’re looking for you to solve complex challenges and shape Space Electronic Warfare by leading our Ground System Architecture, Design, and Development. Your customer will trust you to not only design and develop these systems, but also identify areas requiring urgent mitigation up front and early to develop this system with advanced technology solutions. Share your expertise through leadership and mentoring, while broadening your skillset into areas like continuous software delivery, cloud architecture and services, and cybersecurity. Grow your skills by merging innovative engineering methodologies and cross-disciplinary coordination to create tomorrow’s solutions. Grow your skills by merging software and space based Electronic Warfare to create centralized, modernized, and highly available command and control capabilities. Join our team and create the future of Electronic Warfare for the USSF.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • 10+ years of experience with system engineering supporting space Major Defense Acquisition Programs, such as space, ground, software, or hardware systems

  • 8+ years of experience with DevSecOps and Agile methodologies, the software development life cycle (SDLC), and planning and executing system integration of complex space and ground systems

  • 5+ years of experience architecting and implementing cloud-based solutions and cloud-based development

  • Knowledge of implementation of DevOps and DevSecOps principles focused on automated testing, continuous delivery, real time monitoring and feedback, and security concerns

  • Possession of strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills

  • Master’s degree in an Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or equivalent field

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Top Secret clearance is required.

You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Hollywood Feed was established in the 1950s, in Memphis, TN, as a pet supply store with friendly and knowledgeable service. More than half a century later, our love for pets is who we are today. Our associates are family and the face of each location. We care about each other, our pets, and our customers. Come and experience the passion and drive that makes Hollywood Feed what it is today.

Job Summary
The Third Key Holder, who reports to the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, opens and closes the store, serves customers, and ensures safe, efficient, and profitable operations while upholding Hollywood Feed's first policy: "Do what is right by the customer."
This position offers a competitive hourly wage of $15.50/hr. to $18/hr.

Key Responsibilities
  • Arriving prior to opening and remaining after closing to ensure the store is fully prepared for business operations.
  • Assuming managerial responsibilities in the event of management absences.
  • Greet and assist customers in accordance with Hollywood Feed's established customer service standards.
  • Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of store products to effectively address the needs of both pets and customers.
  • Maintain open and respectful communication with supervisors and coworkers.
  • Work efficiently both independently and as part of a team, providing support and training to new employees.
  • Expected to have open and weekend availability including closing 3 nights per week.

    • Opening and closing registers.
    • Creating customer accounts.
    • Processing customer transactions.

  • Perform additional administrative duties as assigned.

Requirements & Qualifications
  • Commitment to animals and their owners is vital at Hollywood Feed.
  • Strong verbal communication and active listening skills.
  • Proven sales and customer service abilities.
  • Knowledge of store products or ability to learn quickly.
  • Ability to operate or learn the point-of-sale system.

Education & Experience
  • High School Diploma or equivalent

In addition to competitive wages and benefits, retail employees receive tips, and all employees enjoy generous discounts plus free pet food and supplements as Hollywood Feed team members.

title: Director of Operations
description:
The Director of Operations owns the operational performance of Abby's Legendary Pizza's 37 company-owned parlors across Oregon and Central Washington. Reporting directly to the President, this leader owns the four-wall P&L of every parlor: food and paper cost, labor cost, ticket averages, comp and void discipline, food safety, brand standards, and the guest experience that has defined Abby's since 1964. Through 6 district-level leaders (5 District Managers and a Market Coach) and the 37 General Managers with their Associate Manager and Assistant Manager teams, the Director translates brand strategy into consistent, in-store execution while protecting the legacy of "Toppings to the Edge" and 100% real mozzarella.

Header facts

  • Base salary: $135K – $185K
  • Target bonus: 50% of base
  • Travel: ~50–60%
  • Reports to: President

What You'll Do

  • Own the four-wall P&L across all 37 parlors — food and paper cost, labor, prime cost, ticket average, comp and void discipline — and drive same-store sales growth through local-store marketing, LTO execution, and upsell discipline.
  • Lead, coach, and hold accountable 6 district-level leaders (5 District Managers and 1 Market Coach) and, through them, 37 General Managers; rebalance district portfolios as new parlors open.
  • Build the next generation of General Managers, Associate Managers, and Assistant Managers through structured development, in-parlor shadowing, and succession planning.
  • Set and cascade the operating rhythm: pre-shift huddles, weekly one-on-ones with each district leader, monthly regional reviews, and quarterly company-wide scorecard reviews.
  • Partner with Finance on budgeting, forecasting, and capital deployment, and with Marketing on menu engineering, pricing strategy, and LTO rollouts.
  • Own guest-experience metrics — speed of service, order accuracy, online review scores, Net Promoter — across dine-in, carry-out, direct online ordering, and third-party delivery.
  • Champion food safety and compliance: ServSafe certification at all 37 parlors, HACCP-aligned line checks, clean health inspections in both states, OSHA and wage-and-hour compliance, and documented corrective action on every incident.
  • Partner with Real Estate and Facilities on new-parlor openings, remodels, and refreshes, and with Technology on POS, online ordering, loyalty, KDS, scheduling, and inventory tools.

What You Bring

Required

  • 8–12+ years of multi-unit restaurant operations experience, including 3–5 years leading District/Regional Managers (or equivalent) responsible for 25+ company-owned parlors.
  • Verifiable track record of owning four-wall P&L at scale and improving food cost, labor cost, and prime-cost KPIs in pizza, casual dining, or comparable QSR/casual restaurant environment.
  • Demonstrated success opening new company-owned parlors and/or shepherding remodels.
  • Strong working knowledge of ServSafe, HACCP-style daily line checks, and state/county health-department inspection processes.
  • Willingness and ability to travel 50–60% across Oregon and Central Washington; valid driver's license; ability to work evenings and weekends aligned with restaurant operating hours.

Preferred

  • Prior experience operating company-owned restaurant portfolios — direct accountability for staffing and P&L at the store level.
  • Direct experience with pizza, Italian casual dining, or scratch-kitchen concepts.
  • Proven success managing both dine-in and third-party delivery channel economics (DoorDash, Uber Eats).
  • Familiarity with restaurant POS systems and modern scheduling/inventory platforms.
  • Experience working across more than one U.S. state with different labor and health regulations (Oregon and Washington preferred).

Core Attributes & Leadership Traits

This is an enterprise leadership role first. These attributes describe how we expect the Director of Operations to think, lead, and operate across the business:

  • Enterprise Mindset — Thinks about what is best for the brand and company, not one district or parlor; understands how Operations connects to Marketing, HR, Finance, IT, Training, Development, and Supply Chain.
  • Strategic-to-Operational Translator — Turns company strategy into clear field priorities, standards, routines, and measurable results across 37+ parlors.
  • Results & Financial Acumen — Owns sales, traffic, labor, food cost, controllables, and EBITDA; reads a P&L and knows which operational levers drive profitability.
  • Leader of Leaders — Develops and holds District Managers accountable to lead GMs effectively, rather than becoming the person everyone depends upon.
  • High Accountability / High Support — Sets clear expectations, follows up relentlessly, addresses underperformance quickly, and still develops the leaders around them.
  • Systems & Process Orientation — Builds repeatable operating systems instead of relying on heroic individual effort; looks for simplification, consistency, and scale.
  • Change Leadership — Moves Abby’s toward a more disciplined operating model without losing the culture and heritage that make it special.
  • Cross-Functional Influence — Operates as a true member of the executive leadership team — not the head of a silo.
  • Customer & Brand Obsessed — Protects Legendary Pizza and Legendary Hospitality; treats real cheese, toppings to the edge, and freshly rolled dough as working standards, not slogans.
  • Talent Builder — Creates succession depth at DM, GM, and assistant-manager levels; promotes from within and handles under-performance decisively.
  • Data-Driven, Field-Grounded — Uses scorecards and KPIs to find problems, then gets into parlors — pre-shift, peak line, tasting the product — to validate what the numbers are saying.
  • Decisive & Courageous — Makes difficult calls on people, standards, structure, and resources; stays steady in a crisis and owns the next step.
  • Communication & Presence — Communicates credibly from the Board level all the way to a cook, driver, or cashier.
  • Ownership Mentality — Treats Abby’s resources and results as their own business; doesn’t explain away misses, owns them and builds the recovery plan.
  • Multi-State Operator — Comfortable navigating Oregon and Washington labor law, wage rules, predictive scheduling, and differing health-code enforcement styles.

Success Metrics — First 12–18 Months

  • Four-wall EBITDA across the 37-parlor portfolio meets or exceeds annual plan.
  • Portfolio food cost % and labor cost % at or below target; prime cost in the targeted band — achieved consistently across all 6 district portfolios.
  • Same-store sales growth positive and accelerating across the trailing twelve months.
  • Health-department inspection scores at or above target at every parlor; zero critical violations.
  • DM, Market Coach, GM, Associate Manager, and Assistant Manager turnover below industry benchmark; identifiable internal pipeline at every level.
  • New-parlor openings hit 30/60/90-day sales and profitability targets.
  • Guest-experience scores (online reviews, internal guest-comment tracking) trending upward quarter over quarter across all 37 parlors.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $135,000 – $185,000, with a target annual bonus of 50% of base.
  • Health benefits: Medical, dental, vision coverage; life and long-term disability
  • Retirement: 401(k), with company match.
  • Time off & perks: Paid time off, company vehicle, phone stipend.

Working Conditions & ADA

Field-heavy role. Ability to be on the road 50–60% of the time visiting the 37 parlors across the 6 district portfolios; ability to stand for extended periods during restaurant visits; ability to lift up to 30 lbs (e.g., food and supply deliveries in support of operational reviews); willingness to work evenings and weekends aligned with restaurant operating hours; ability to respond to operational emergencies outside of normal business hours.

title: GIS Technician
description:
Description

Under general supervision, performs technical GIS work to develop, maintain, and improve the Town’s geographic information resources. Creates and maintains GIS data; performs quality assurance and quality control; produces maps and other cartographic products; researches and integrates data; and provides support for GIS applications and workflows. Collaborates with Town departments to provide accurate geographic information that supports municipal operations, planning, and decision-making.

Examples of Duties

Examples of Duties

  • Create, edit, maintain, and quality-check GIS data, databases, feature classes, and map layers.
  • Interpret and incorporate information from plats, deeds, legal descriptions, engineering plans, as-built drawings, and other source materials into GIS.
  • Develop clear, accurate, and useful maps and other GIS products for internal and external customers.
  • Research, analyze, and integrate GIS and related data from a variety of sources.
  • Support GIS data collection, verification, and maintenance in office and field environments as needed.
  • Assist with web-based and enterprise GIS resources, including maps, applications, and data services.
  • Respond to GIS questions and service requests by helping users find, understand, and use geographic information.
  • Work with Town departments to understand business needs and identify practical GIS solutions.
  • Perform data quality assurance and quality control and help maintain standards for accuracy, consistency, and usability.
  • Create and maintain documentation, metadata, procedures, and other resources that support reliable GIS operations.
  • Assist with GIS-related projects, process improvements, automation, technology evaluations, and other initiatives as assigned.
  • Stay current with GIS technologies, methods, and practices and share knowledge with teammates and customers.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Minimum of 1 year of education, training, certification, or experience in GIS, geography, planning, information technology, or a related field sufficient to perform the essential functions of the position.
  • Minimum of 1 year of hands on experience using GIS software and working with geographic data, mapping, or related technology.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, provide quality customer service, and work collaboratively with others.
  • Valid Texas driver’s license and driving record in compliance with Town policy.

Physical Abilities
The physical abilities described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.*
  • To perform essential functions of the job must be able to read, write, talk, see and hear.
  • Operate various office equipment, push, pull and/or lift equipment and supplies, lift and carry up to 50 pounds.

* Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Desired Qualifications

Desired Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree or higher in GIS, geography, planning, computer science, information technology, or a related field.
  • Two years of progressively responsible experience in ArcPro/ArcGIS Online.
  • Experience with Esri ArcGIS Pro and/or ArcGIS Online.
  • Experience with ArcGIS Enterprise or other enterprise GIS environments.
  • Experience working with municipal, utility, infrastructure, property, addressing, or public works GIS data.
  • Experience interpreting plats, deeds, legal descriptions, engineering plans, or as-built drawings.
  • Experience with GIS field data collection, GPS, databases, CAD, or asset management systems.
  • Experience with GIS data quality assurance/quality control, documentation, or workflow improvement.

Knowledge/ Skills / Abilities
  • Working knowledge of GIS concepts, spatial data, cartography, and data management practices.
  • Ability to accurately edit, analyze, organize, and maintain GIS data.
  • Ability to interpret technical source documents and translate information into GIS.
  • Ability to troubleshoot problems, research solutions, and learn new technologies.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and quality.
  • Ability to communicate technical information clearly to both GIS and non-GIS users.
  • Ability to organize work, manage competing priorities, and complete assignments independently and as part of a team.
  • Willingness to occasionally work outside normal business hours or in the field when operational needs require.

This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

Especialista de Tecnologia da Informação

Um futuro mais saudável. É isso que nos motiva a inovar. Promover continuamente a ciência e garantir que todos tenham acesso à assistência médica de que precisam hoje e pelas próximas gerações. Criar um mundo onde todos nós temos mais tempo com as pessoas que amamos. É isso que nos faz Roche.

Este profissional será responsável pela implementação de softwares, automação de processos e gestão da governança ágil, atuando de forma consultiva para apoiar o sucesso do cliente e as estratégias comerciais. O candidato ideal deve unir alta capacidade analítica para resolução de problemas complexos com um perfil ético e inovador, focado em mitigar riscos técnicos e maximizar o valor das nossas soluções de diagnóstico no mercado.

Sobre a Oportunidade:

  • Realizar instalação, atualização e manutenção de sistemas de informação em campo e no cliente.

  • Atuar como segundo nível de suporte local, interagindo com especialistas e escalonando falhas para instâncias globais (Latam/GCS) quando necessário.

  • Gestão de Treinamentos: Capacitar clientes, distribuidores e equipes internas nas soluções tecnológicas da companhia.

  • Identificar riscos técnicos ou de negócio nas contas e conduzir planos de ação preventivos e testes específicos.

  • Executar atividades de Customer Success para fornecer visibilidade estratégica às áreas de Vendas e Produto.

  • Apoiar oportunidades de workflow e TI, validando requisitos técnicos em editais e concorrências públicas.

  • Realizar demonstrações técnicas das soluções digitais e construir protótipos (mini-apps) para viabilizar projetos.

  • Mapear oportunidades nas contas e direcionar à força de vendas para projetos de Consultoria Laboratorial.

Quem você é:

  • Graduação em TI, Ciência da Computação, Análise de Sistemas ou áreas correlatas (Diferencial: Pós-graduação e certificações em Agile, UX ou Customer Success).
  • Sólidos conhecimentos em redes de computadores, segurança da informação, web services e protocolos de comunicação (ASTM, HL7).
  • Experiência em administração e manutenção de bancos de dados (Oracle, Intersystems Caché, MySQL ou SQL Server).
  • Experiência com servidores virtualizados/Cloud (AWS) e vivência em processos laboratoriais ou hospitalares.
  • Perfil proativo e resolutivo, com visão sistêmica e orientação total ao cliente.
  • Domínio de metodologias ágeis e capacidade de autogestão para atuar de forma independente.
  • Habilidade para trabalhar com equipes diversas e remotas, mantendo comunicação fluida em todos os níveis da organização.
  • Inglês e espanhol avançados para conversação e colaboração ativa com times internacionais.
  • Flexibilidade para atuar fora do horário comercial e disponibilidade para viagens nacionais e internacionais.
  • Possuir Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (Categoria B).

Os benefícios de realocação não estão disponíveis para essa posição.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.


Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

AI Builder, Emerging Talent - Italian Market


Technical foundation required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.


Salesforce is hiring AI Builders, people who are early in their career but not early in their ambition. As part of our first-of-its-kind AI Builder New Grad cohort, you'll be embedded directly with customer-facing teams, designing, developing, and deploying Agentic solutions for the world’s Fortune 500. We are at the beginning of the agentic era, and you will be at the keyboard building the solutions that define how the world's largest companies operate. You’ll deliver real-time customer impact from day one. Working in a builder pod, a cross-functional team that collaborates to design, build, and deploy AI solutions for real customers. It's a built-in support system to ensure you're set up to win. Honestly, you're already thinking about what you'd build here…

You’ll be paired with a dedicated onboarding buddy and have the opportunity to partner with senior developers.
  • Skill Acceleration: This role is designed to develop both your technical depth and your sales skills, ensuring you can lead high-level conversations with stakeholders.

  • Develop AI agents that take real actions for real companies. This is not a side project. Agentforce is live, in production, running for some of the biggest companies on the planet.
  • Design Agent Intelligence: Design how agents think: prompts, reasoning, tool calls, and the entire architecture, leveraging AI/LLM technologies and the Agentforce platform.
  • Support the entire Technical Lifecycle: Collaborate with other Builders to architect, build, debug, and deploy high-quality, scalable production systems using JavaScript, Python, and Apex.
  • Drive Strategic Impact: Partner with clients to turn business challenges into agentic solutions. You’ll use your consultative skills to ensure our tech meets real-world needs
  • Iterate and Deploy: Test it, break it, fix it, ship it. Repeat. You will own your work from day one.

You’re Our Builder If…

  • You have a strong background in Computer Science or a related engineering discipline.
  • You’re an AI native who has been deep in LLMs and prompt engineering.
  • You are fluent in React, TypeScript, GraphQL, Python, OOP and Real-Time Infra
  • You can hold your own in a room with our sales teams and customers.
  • You write high-quality code and evaluate AI outputs with engineering rigor.
  • You thrive in the group chat that’s building something, not just talking about it.
  • You're ready to grow faster here than anywhere else - nobody has 10 years of experience in this new frontier, which means your ideas carry real weight from day one.
  • You bring sharp problem-solving instincts, relentless initiative, and a get-things-done mentality.
  • You are excited to travel 25-50% of the time, working directly alongside our customers to see your code come to life in their environments.
  • You are fluent in Italian and English


Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist - Fixed Term Contract

Slater and Gordon Lawyers are a leading personal injury and class actions law firm where every member of our team has a shared passion for our clients: we are people caring for people. Our commitment to our people includes offering genuine work-life balance, with a hybrid work environment allowing them to split their time between home and the office. We recognise and reward high performance and have outstanding employee benefits including a week of shutdown leave, paid parental leave, extra-long service leave, together with various ongoing learning and professional development opportunities.

Position Overview

The Data Scientist is responsible for rectifying master data issues, testing data and NLP solutions, and supporting the engineering team to implement NLP techniques in real-time systems. The role combines data-quality expertise, advanced testing capability and practical NLP knowledge to improve the accuracy, consistency and reliability of data-driven products.

Key Accountabilities

- Investigate and rectify master data issues, including duplicates, inaccurate records, inconsistent values, missing information and broken relationships.
- Define data-quality rules, remediation approaches and controls with data owners and business stakeholders.
- Profile datasets and identify root causes of data-quality issues across source systems and integrations.
- Design and execute comprehensive testing for data pipelines, remediation processes, NLP models, APIs and real-time system integrations.
- Develop test cases, test data, validation criteria and regression test suites, and document defects and outcomes clearly.
- Apply NLP techniques such as entity extraction, classification, similarity matching and language models to improve data processing and quality.
- Work closely with engineers to translate NLP concepts into reliable, scalable and maintainable real-time implementations.
- Evaluate NLP outputs for accuracy, latency, robustness, explainability, privacy and suitability for production use.
- Coordinate priorities, decisions and remediation activities with data owners, engineers, subject-matter experts and other stakeholders.

Experience and qualifications

- Tertiary qualification in data science, computer science, statistics, mathematics, artificial intelligence or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
- Experience rectifying master data and data-quality issues across multiple systems or datasets.
- Experience designing and executing structured testing for data pipelines, APIs, machine learning models or real-time systems.
- Practical experience applying NLP techniques to business or operational data.
-Experience working with engineers and stakeholders to deliver production-ready data or analytics solutions.
-Experience handling sensitive information in accordance with privacy, security and governance requirements.

What next?

If you are interested in this opportunity, please apply directly to Slater and Gordon. We prefer to talk with you personally and are not accepting applications from recruitment agencies.

To be eligible for this position, you must be an Australian citizen, a permanent resident, or hold a valid visa with full and unrestricted working rights in Australia. Proof of work rights will be required as part of the Slater and Gordon application process.
