Slater and Gordon is an equal opportunity employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other legally protected attributes. We understand that everyone has different needs. If you require reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process, please let us know in your application.

title: Floor Staff - Matinee, Nights, and Weekends
description:
Team members are classified based on individual theatre needs, and/or employee availability, as either variable hour, part-time fixed, part-time regular or full-time hourly employees whose primary responsibility is ensuring our guests receive exceptional service. Team members may be scheduled to work in the Box Office, Concession Stand, or as an Usher. Team members employees must act as a representative of Regal in a way that is consistent with our mission statement and policies; including

  • Regular and consistent attendance
  • Handling of emergency situations when called upon to do so
  • General cleaning duties; and
  • Compliance with our company dress code.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities for each position include, but are not limited to, the following:

Box Office

  • Operating POS system, including the proper handling of and responsibility for accuracy of cash drawer, credit cards, travelers’ checks, gift cards and redeemed discount tickets, passes and coupons
  • Up selling/suggestive selling of Premium Viewing Experience (3D, RPX, IMAX).

Concession

In addition, you must complete the Regal Responsible Beverage Server training on Regal Online University.

Language Ability:

Possess good public speaking, listen effectively and respond clearly and directly.

Math Ability:

Perform calculations with speed and accuracy and identify and correct errors.

Reasoning Ability:

Identify problems, gather relevant data and note possible causes of problems. Evaluate relevant information, recognize alternatives and reach conclusions based on evidence. Take action beyond what is necessarily called for. Perform under pressure and/or opposition.

Personal Skills:

Possess excellent communication skills with customers, co-workers and management. Establish goals, budget time, and set priorities to achieve desired objectives.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

description:
BrightQuest Treatment Center in Nashville, TN is hiring a Lead Dietitian!

BrightQuest is an organization dedicated to providing highly specialized treatment serving individuals and families suffering from complex mental illness and co-occurring disorders. Our vision at BrightQuest is to provide best in class treatment founded on a therapeutic community model that provides a supportive environment for social skills development and reparative attachment experiences. Our mission is to provide hope, strength and inspiration for individuals and families suffering from mental health, co-occurring, and substance use disorders so that they can heal, transform their lives, and realize all the possibilities of a life in recovery. We value our employees and contractors, and our goal is to engage those who share our core values and our vision.

The Dietitian supports our clients in optimizing nutrition to benefit physical and mental health, often collaborating with other team members to achieve this. The Dietitian plays a key role in identifying clients who may benefit from addition of the Nutrition Program to their treatment plan.

Primary Purpose and Function

The Lead Dietitian supports client in optimizing nutrition to benefit physical and mental health, often collaborating with other team members to achieve this. The Lead Dietitian plays a key role in identifying clients who may benefit from addition of the Nutrition Program (individual medical nutrition therapy sessions and nutrition group).

  • Document sessions using Academy of Nutrition and Dietetic nutrition care process (PES format).

title: LN Venues, Lead AI Engineer – Finance Transformation
description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit .

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!

THE JOB

Venue Nation is seeking a technical leader to help transform how our Finance organization operates - from automating complex workflows to enabling smarter decision-making at scale. You will partner directly with Finance leadership and Accounting teams to identify high-impact opportunities, then design and build the AI-powered solutions that deliver on them, spanning financial reporting, close, reconciliation, and forecasting.

This is a builder-leader role: your code ships to production, and your technical judgment shapes how AI is applied across the finance function. Based within Venue Nation Analytics alongside our Data Science team, you will own solutions from discovery through production. Your work will span a growing portfolio of projects sponsored by the Division CFO. We are looking for a self-starter who brings structure to undefined problems - someone who can break down a business process as readily as they can architect an agent.

WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

Build and Ship

  • Design and build AI-powered solutions across the accounting lifecycle, from high-volume transactional work (invoice coding, cash application, account reconciliations, journal-entry support, and close-task coordination) to management reporting, forecasting, and decision support.
  • Apply LLMs, RAG, and agentic workflows to real business problems, selecting the right approach for each use case.
  • Stand up pilots in development environments to validate solutions with business users and partner with Data Services to deploy to production.
  • Collaborate with the Data Science team to apply AI to forecasting and planning workflows, including variance detection and driver analysis.

Partner and Discover

  • Partner with Finance leadership and operational finance teams to understand how work is done today and decompose workflows to identify where AI can assist.
  • Serve as a translator between finance and technical stakeholders, ensuring solutions reflect how the business actually works.

Build for Trust and Auditability

  • Develop evaluation frameworks that measure solution accuracy and reliability against defined thresholds, and produce the documentation needed to meet Finance governance and audit requirements.
  • Design human-in-the-loop review workflows, exception handling, and confidence-based routing so that AI-enabled solutions earn trust incrementally.
  • Ensure financial calculations are performed through deterministic, auditable logic rather than generative outputs.

Compound the Capability

  • Contribute reusable components, patterns, and best practices that accelerate AI delivery across the Analytics organization.
  • Monitor deployed solutions for accuracy drift, performance, cost, and adoption, and iterate based on what you learn.

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of professional engineering experience, including 3+ years designing and delivering production LLM-based applications and agentic workflows, with demonstrated technical leadership.
  • Experience applying AI, machine learning, or advanced automation to finance or accounting processes.
  • Solid understanding of finance and accounting concepts, including P&L structure, close and reporting processes, and how financial results relate to underlying transactional data.
  • Full-stack development experience, with the ability to build and ship user-facing applications and review interfaces (e.g., React, Streamlit, or similar) without relying on a separate front-end team.
  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building against modern cloud data platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate independently in ambiguous environments - defining scope, prioritizing, and delivering outcomes without dedicated project management support.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and finance audiences and present clearly to senior leadership.

Preferred

  • Experience with Databricks (Apps, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Genie) or a comparable lakehouse platform.
  • Experience integrating with ERP and Accounting systems of record.
  • Background in a multi-unit operating business such as live entertainment, hospitality, or retail.
  • Master's degree in a related field.

BENEFITS & PERKS

Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits:

HEALTH: Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA)

YOURSELF: Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days

WEALTH: 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program

FAMILY: New parent programs including caregiver leave, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support

CAREER: Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment

OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We aspire to build teams that reflect and support the fans and artists we serve. Every day we aim to promote environments where everyone can be themselves, contribute fully, and thrive within our company and at our events. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with.


Live Nation strongly supports equal employment opportunity for all applicants regardless of age (40 and over), ancestry, color, religious creed (including religious dress and grooming practices), family and medical care leave or the denial of family and medical care leave, mental or physical disability (including HIV and AIDS), marital status, domestic partner status, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), genetic information, military and veteran status, political affiliation, national origin (including language use restrictions), citizenship, race, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding), gender, gender identity, and gender expression, sexual orientation, intersectionality, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law, rule, ordinance or regulation.

We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Los Angeles Fair Chance Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act and consistent with other similar and / or applicable laws in other areas.

We also afford equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with a disability. For this reason, Live Nation will make reasonable accommodations for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability who is an applicant consistent with its legal obligations to do so, including reasonable accommodations related to pregnancy in accordance with applicable local, state and / or federal law. As part of its commitment to make reasonable accommodations, Live Nation also wishes to participate in a timely, good faith, interactive process with a disabled applicant to determine effective reasonable accommodations, if any, which can be made in response to a request for accommodations. Applicants are invited to identify reasonable accommodations that can be made to assist them to perform the essential functions of the position they seek. title: IT Support Specialist
description:

The Help Desk and IT Support Specialist serves as the primary point of contact for employee technology support and resolves day-to-day IT issues across a multi-location environment. The role requires ownership of assigned requests from initial contact through resolution, including troubleshooting, user communication, documentation, follow-up, and appropriate escalation. The specialist also assists with onboarding and offboarding, device deployment, asset management, endpoint maintenance, and IT documentation.

Key Responsibilities

As a Machine Learning Engineer on the Digital Experience Insights team, you'll help take machine learning models from prototype to production, building the pipelines, infrastructure, and engineering practices that let models run reliably at scale. title: Senior Scientist- Cancer immunology/immunotherapy
description:
We are seeking a highly motivated and scientifically driven Senior Scientist- Cancer immunology/immunotherapy with deep expertise in cancer immunology and immunotherapy to join our Oncology research team. The successful candidate will bring extensive experience in T cell biology, neoantigen discovery, immunopeptidomics, and immune function assessment in both in vitro and in vivo systems, with a particular interest in cancer vaccine development. You will independently design and execute complex research studies, troubleshoot and optimize experimental approaches, and generate high-quality scientific data that advances our understanding of anti-tumor immune responses and enables the development of novel immunotherapeutic strategies.

As a Senior Scientist, you will be a key contributor within a multidisciplinary team focused on antigen discovery, target validation, and the development of approaches to induce and enhance anti-tumor immunity. Leveraging your expertise in immunology, you will establish and apply advanced assay systems, collaborate across discovery and development teams, and deliver critical datasets that directly impact oncology drug discovery programs and the advancement of innovative cancer therapies.

Accountabilities

  • Independently design, execute, and interpret mechanistic cancer immunology and drug discovery studies utilizing immunological, molecular, and cellular biology techniques.
  • Drive antigen discovery and validation efforts to support the development of novel cancer immunotherapies and vaccine approaches.
  • Assess, analyze, and communicate experimental data with minimal supervision while understanding its broader relevance to drug discovery and development objectives.
  • Apply scientific expertise to investigate vaccine-induced immune responses, T cell biology, antigen presentation pathways, and mechanisms that influence immunogenicity.
  • Establish, optimize, and implement innovative in vitro assay systems to evaluate immune responses and therapeutic candidates.
  • Collaborate effectively across programs and departments, sharing scientific knowledge and providing experimental insight to accelerate research progress.
  • Maintain comprehensive and accurate experimental documentation and ensure compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), Safety, Health and Environment standards, AstraZeneca policies, and applicable regulations.
  • Contribute to scientific strategy discussions, project planning, and experimental design across multiple oncology research programs.
  • Lead or co-lead project teams as required and contribute to scientific publication, presentation, and intellectual property objectives.
  • Stay informed of emerging scientific advancements in immunology, oncology, and cancer vaccines, integrating new knowledge into research approaches.

Essential Skills/Experience

  • Master's degree or equivalent experience, in Immunology or a related scientific discipline, with a minimum of 2 years of relevant postdoctoral, biotechnology, or pharmaceutical industry experience.
  • Extensive expertise in T cell biology, antigen-presenting cell (APC) function, and immune-mediated mechanisms relevant to cancer immunotherapy.
  • Strong understanding of cancer vaccine technologies and approaches to generating anti-tumor immune responses.
  • Experience assessing and characterizing T cell immune responses using a variety of functional and phenotypic assays.
  • Experience designing and conducting antigen screening and validation studies.
  • Experience with immunopeptidomics and antigen discovery technologies is highly desirable.
  • Hands-on expertise in immunological and biochemical techniques, including multi-parameter flow cytometry (FACS), ELISA, multiplex cytokine assays, ELISpot, western blotting, luminescence-based assays, cell killing assays, and high-content imaging.
  • Experience with TCR cloning, engineering, and expression methodologies.
  • Strong data analysis and scientific interpretation skills with the ability to communicate complex findings effectively.
  • Excellent organizational, collaboration, and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities and timelines.
  • Proven scientific track record demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and other scientific contributions.

Desirable Skills/Experience

  • Experience performing in vitro T cell functional characterization, including antigen specificity, activation, proliferation, and cytotoxicity assessments.
  • Hands-on expertise with murine tumor models and in vivo immuno-oncology studies.
  • Experience developing, evaluating, or advancing cancer vaccine platforms.
  • Experience working with human tissues and primary patient-derived samples.
  • Knowledge of neoantigen discovery workflows and translational immunology approaches.
  • Experience supporting oncology drug discovery and preclinical development programs within a pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment.
  • Familiarity with bioinformatics approaches associated with immunopeptidomics, antigen discovery, or immune monitoring datasets.

title: Patent Agent, Hardware
description:
About Hark

Hark is an artificial intelligence company building advanced, personalized intelligence. One that is proactive, multimodal, and capable of interacting with the world through speech, text, vision, and persistent memory.

We're pairing that intelligence with next-generation hardware to create a universal interface between humans and machines. While today's AI largely operates through chat boxes and decade-old devices, Hark is focused on what comes next: agentic systems that interact naturally with people and the real world.

To get there, we're developing multimodal models and next-generation AI hardware together - designed from the ground up as a single, unified interface for a new era of intelligent systems.

About the Role

Hark is seeking a Patent Agent to build the hardware side of our patent portfolio from the ground up. This person will own invention harvesting, drafting, and prosecution across our hardware technologies, and will shape how the company decides what to protect as its products move from architecture to prototype to production.

This role sits inside Legal but lives with engineering. You will be in design reviews and prototype reviews, sitting with electrical, mechanical, systems, firmware, and product design engineers, finding the inventions before anyone has thought to write them down. Then you will go draft the applications yourself.

A strong portfolio is not measured by the number of patents filed. It requires knowing which technologies will matter most, anticipating how products and competitors will evolve, and obtaining claims that protect the underlying innovation rather than one implementation of it. This is a hands-on opportunity for someone who wants to author that strategy rather than inherit it.

Responsibilities

  • Build and execute the patent strategy for Hark's hardware products and platform technologies, including portfolio architecture across core, platform, and product-specific innovations
  • Work directly with electrical, mechanical, systems, firmware, wireless, sensor, and product design engineers to identify patentable inventions
  • Draft and prosecute U.S. and international applications covering hardware and hardware-software systems, translating complex engineering into technically accurate and strategically broad claims
  • Prepare office action responses, conduct examiner interviews, and develop prosecution strategies aimed at commercially meaningful claim scope
  • Manage continuation, divisional, and design patent strategy as products and architectures evolve
  • Review and improve applications prepared by outside counsel, and work with international counsel on PCT and foreign prosecution strategy
  • Conduct patentability and prior art analyses, monitor competitive patent activity, and support freedom-to-operate work ahead of product milestones
  • Own inventorship determinations, assignment hygiene, and IDS practice across the portfolio

Requirements

  • Registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, with an active registration number
  • Bachelor's degree or higher in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or a closely related technical discipline
  • 5+ years drafting and prosecuting patent applications involving complex hardware technologies, at a firm, in-house, or both
  • Experience at a consumer electronics, hardware, semiconductor, wearable, mobile device, or AI hardware company — you know what happens to a patent strategy when an architecture changes late in a build
  • You can take an engineer's half-formed disclosure and turn it into a complete application, claims and figures included, without supervision
  • Strong command of electrical, mechanical, and systems-level engineering concepts, and the confidence to push an inventor on the details
  • Comfortable building in ambiguity — you've stood up prosecution processes from scratch, not just inherited them
  • Hands-on by default; you're drafting, not just managing outside counsel
  • Excellent written communication and exceptional attention to technical detail

Bonus Qualifications

  • Design patent practice for consumer products, and coordination between utility and design filings
  • Experience managing substantial international portfolios across multiple jurisdictions
  • Competitive patent landscaping and freedom-to-operate analysis
  • Engineering experience prior to entering patent practice, or an advanced technical degree

Compensation

The US base salary range for this full-time position is between $150,000 – $220,000 annually.

The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package may also include additional components/benefits depending on the specific role. This information will be shared if an employment offer is extended. (edited)

You will set the benchmark for digital excellence by anticipating consumer behaviour, leveraging emerging technologies, and embedding best-practice approaches across eCommerce. Harnessing insights from data and market trends, you’ll evolve MECCA’s digital capability while fostering a culture of innovation and collaboration.

You will also bring:

Our market opportunity is rare in its scale and powered by a strong business model, first-rate investors and advisors, and a global product management team (if we do say so ourselves). Clio is growing rapidly, and Product Managers here grow their scope as we open new markets.

Speaking of Product at Clio, we have worked hard to develop an excellent product management culture with empowered PMs who carry real influence across the organization. Our team brings together seasoned professionals from a diverse set of product backgrounds. Clio invests heavily in developing Product Managers, growing leaders, and in the broader Product communities in which we operate.

What you'll work on:

As a Senior Product Manager, and in conjunction with your Development and Design counterparts (your triad), you will drive successful outputs and outcomes across Clio's portfolio in Italy.

End to End Portfolio Ownership:

  • You own Clio's product portfolio and customer experience in Italy end to end, from first touch through onboarding, daily practice management, billing, and support. Where a gap sits in a product another team owns, you own getting it closed.

  • You are accountable for the quality of Clio's customer experience in Italy as a whole, rather than for a single feature area. Your measure of success is whether a lawyer in Italy can run their practice on Clio without hitting a wall that a lawyer in North America would not hit.

  • You maintain a single, current view of what breaks today, what is missing, and what we have committed for Italy, and you make that view legible to leadership before leadership asks for it.

Product Leadership and Execution:

  • Working from the overarching strategy set by your Senior Director, Product Management, you will develop a roadmap in conjunction with your peers that moves our business forward, and evangelize it throughout the company.

  • You will own the delivery of features in the roadmap while also ensuring they deliver on the desired business outcome.

  • Drive product readiness for the Italian market, including localization, multi-lingual support, regulatory requirements, and market-specific workflows.

Speed and Iteration Toward a Clear Vision:

  • You set a clear vision for what Clio looks like in Italy, then ship toward it in weeks rather than quarters. We expect a first customer-visible change within your first 90 days.

  • You will make decisions with imperfect information, put something in front of customers, and correct from what you learn. We aim to validate with real customers before building at scale, however there are scenarios where a regulatory deadline sets the date. In those cases we will commit to the date and narrow the scope rather than move the date.

  • You parallelize. When a workstream can run alongside another, you run it alongside, and you say what serializing would cost in weeks when you choose to serialize.

Local Legal Market Understanding:

  • You understand how lawyers in Italy actually work: how Italian civil law shapes a firm's structure, how matters progress through the local courts, how the profession sets and regulates fees, what the Consiglio Nazionale Forense and the local Ordini require of a practitioner, and where local practice diverges from common law practice.

  • You track the regulatory surface that touches our product, including Italian electronic invoicing through SdI, split payment VAT, and Consiglio Nazionale Forense professional rules, and you translate it into requirements our central teams can build against.

  • You build and maintain direct relationships with practitioners, bar associations, and local partners, and you serve as the company's source of truth on what the Italian legal profession needs.

System Design and Technical Fluency:

  • You can read and reason about how we built our platform: where our data models carry a country assumption, how the model represents currency, tax, payments, and locale, and what a change to one of those costs downstream.

  • You can hold a design discussion with engineering about cardinality, extensibility, and migration, and leave with a shared decision.

  • You can tell a problem that needs a local configuration from a problem that needs a platform capability, and you argue for the platform capability when it is the right answer.

AI Native Working Style:

  • You work AI-first by default. You use AI for customer research synthesis, competitive and regulatory analysis, requirements drafting, data querying, and prototyping, and you can show how it changed your throughput.

  • You build your own working systems. You are comfortable writing prompts, chaining tools, and standing up a lightweight agent or script to remove repetitive work from your week.

  • You bring judgment to it. You know which AI output needs verification against a primary source, particularly on regulatory and legal questions, and you verify it.

Influencing Central Teams:

  • Central teams build the platform that Italy depends on, and their leadership sets their goals, metrics, and roadmap without Italy in them. Your job is to quantify the case for Italy well enough that it wins a place on that roadmap.

  • You will build the business case in the currency that team's leadership measures it on, name the tradeoff you are asking them to make, and find the version of the ask that serves their goal alongside yours.

  • You escalate on a stated trigger rather than on frustration. When merit alone does not win the ask, you bring your Senior Director a clear recommendation and the cost of inaction.

Cross-Functional Partnership:

  • Partner closely with cross-functional leaders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Operations to support the Italian market launch and growth.

  • Manage stakeholder relationships across a matrixed organization with clarity and diplomacy.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in Italian and in English. Clio operates in English, so English fluency is a requirement of the role rather than a preference.

  • 4-5 years of experience in product management

  • Working knowledge of the Italian legal market, including Italian civil law, how local firms operate, and the regulatory requirements that apply to them

  • Proven track record of independently taking multiple products or features from ideation to launch in a SaaS environment

  • Experience owning a product area end to end, including outcomes that depended on teams outside your own

  • Demonstrated expertise in localization and multi-lingual product development. This is a core requirement for the role.

  • Experience building or managing multilingual applications or internationalization projects, and expanding products to other countries and languages

  • Technical fluency sufficient to reason about system design, data models, and platform tradeoffs with engineering

  • A demonstrated AI-native working style, with specific examples of how you use AI in your product practice

  • Evidence of winning roadmap commitments from teams that do not report to you and that carry no accountability for your outcome

  • Exceptional attention to detail, so that no requirement or specification slips through the product development cycle

  • Outstanding organizational skills, capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously without compromising quality or timelines

  • Experience using data to inform decisions without succumbing to analysis paralysis

  • Genuine ability to put yourself in our customers' shoes and operate from a place of empathy

  • Experience working across time zones and cultures, with a customer-first approach

  • An entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in ambiguity

  • At least 2 or 3 failures under your belt, the learnings of which you can bring to Clio

  • Ability to work in a highly collaborative team without ego

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Serious bonus points if you:

  • Have prior experience in legal tech, or a strong understanding of the legal services market, including familiarity with legal practice management software and the needs of legal professionals

  • Have worked directly with Consiglio Nazionale Forense and the local Ordini or comparable professional bodies

  • Worked previously in a regulated industry or with multi-product ecosystems

  • Have shipped against a regulatory deadline in Italy or another EU market

  • Successfully launched products in global markets

  • Have a track record of breaking down objectives into initiatives and delivering to customers at scale

  • Have built internal tooling or agents to support your own product practice

  • Demonstrable experience self-serving answers, insights, and data from a variety of data analytics tools

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

  • Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits and dental coverage

  • Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.

  • Flexible time off policy

  • Pension contribution

  • Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

​

The expected salary range for this role is €90,200 to €122,000 EUR. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

Disclaimer: We only communicate with candidates through official @clio.com email addresses.

title: Data Engineer, Accounting
description:
MONTICELLOAM, LLC and its affiliates (“Monticello”) is a real estate and asset-based lender providing asset management and comprehensive capital solutions for healthcare, multifamily, and commercial real estate assets throughout the US. MonticelloAM is seeking team players who can work in a collaborative environment and possess drive, integrity, creativity, compassion, and a strong work ethic.

We're looking for a Financial Accounting Operations Data Engineer to build and maintain the data and reporting platform behind our accounting and treasury operations — from system integrations and ingestion pipelines to warehouse modeling, financial reporting, and the internal tooling that streamlines workflows across accounting and treasury operations.

This role is fully in person. Candidates must be able to work onsite at our office location.

Our Tech Stack

At Monticello, we build and operate our data platform using modern, scalable technologies. In this role, you’ll work hands-on with:

Application Development

  • Kyriba and NetSuite as the core treasury and accounting systems we integrate with
  • Ramp as the AP system we integrate with
  • Python for backend services, APIs, automation, and data engineering
  • REST APIs that deliver data and tooling to business users

Data Platform

  • Snowflake as our cloud data warehouse
  • dbt for modular, version-controlled data transformations
  • Airflow for orchestration and workflow automation
  • SQL for data modeling and analysis

Infrastructure & Delivery

  • AWS for cloud infrastructure and services
  • Docker and CI/CD pipelines for automated, reliable deployment
  • Git for version control and CI/CD

About Your Team

You'll join an entrepreneurial, collaborative team that builds the data, reporting, and analytics systems powering our accounting and treasury operations. You'll work closely with business stakeholders and our offshore development teams to turn requirements into delivered solutions. Each team member owns their solutions, beyond just the technical implementation.

What you'll own:

  • Serving as the primary engineering resource for Kyriba and NetSuite enhancements, integrations, and day-to-day support, helping accounting and treasury teams identify opportunities to improve workflows and reduce manual work.
  • Designing and building the data pipelines that bring data from all our systems into a single, reliable source of truth (Snowflake, Airflow, dbt)
  • Building and maintaining the data pipelines and processes supporting accounting and treasury operations – including GL coding, bank account reconciliation and financial statement reporting
  • Translate feedback from accounting, treasury, and FP&A teams to SQL based data quality rules
  • Developing the React based dashboards that support day-to-day accounting and portfolio decisions

You'll also contribute to:

  • Evolving our data models and warehouse architecture
  • Data quality frameworks and automated QC processes
  • Deployment, CI/CD, and monitoring that keep our systems running reliably

Qualifications

Core:

  • Deep familiarity with NetSuite and Kyriba, and experience building integrations that connect them.
  • Familiarity with accounting and/or treasury concepts
  • Experience building and deploying software end to end – from concept through production
  • Strong Python skills across data engineering, backend services, and APIs
  • Hands-on experience building data pipelines and transformations (Airflow, dbt, or similar)
  • Experience with cloud data warehouses (Snowflake preferred) and strong SQL
  • Experience pulling and wrangling data from REST APIs and third-party systems

Also valuable:

  • DevOps experience – Docker, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and AWS
  • Experience working directly with non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience building deeply interactive dashboards in React

We welcome applicants from a variety of educational and professional backgrounds. If you've built and shipped software and are looking to own projects end to end, we'd like to hear from you – even if your experience doesn't match every bullet.

What We Value

  • A strong team player who thrives in a collaborative environment
  • Excellent communication – a good listener asks insight-generating questions
  • Comfortable being uncomfortable – able to navigate ambiguity and rapid change
  • An entrepreneurial mindset – be willing to take a risk on something new to improve the business, not just prescribed work
  • An ability to respectfully disagree with each other in pursuit of a common goal

At Monticello, we believe that finding creative solutions for our clients comes from the collaboration of people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives. We strive to build an inclusive work environment that celebrates differences and empowers all individuals with opportunities to channel their entrepreneurial spirit. Monticello is an EEO employer.

Monticello offers a competitive base salary and bonus. The base salary range for this position is $100,000-$140,000/year. The specific compensation that will be offered is based on an understanding of the hired candidate's qualifications at the time of hire. Employees are eligible for a discretionary bonus based on employee work performance reviewed during the annual review process.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Opal Security:

At Opal, we’re building modern identity governance for the AI era—intelligent access management that empowers enterprises to move fast while staying secure. Our mission is to bring clarity, control, and confidence to complex enterprise environments, helping teams govern access without slowing down innovation.

About the Role:

Identity is having a moment. Every company is deploying agents, spinning up service accounts, and realizing their IAM stack can't keep up. We're building AI-native security that scales with this chaos and companies like Databricks and Figma are betting on us to get it right.

You will build customer solutions across the entire stack. You'll talk directly to security and eng teams at Fortune 500s and startups alike, understand their messy reality, and architect systems that actually solve their problems. You'll own the problem, not just the solution, which means you get to be creative, challenge assumptions, and build things that don't exist yet.

This is a team of people who genuinely like each other and want to work together. We value thoughtful engineering over speed-running tickets. You'll collaborate with people who have wildly different expertise, debate tradeoffs, and ship work you're proud of.

Please note: We've built a team that works exceptionally well together and has fun doing so. We're looking to bring on new teammates who will both add to and grow with what we're building

Your Responsibilities:

  • Own critical product areas from concept to production: design and build features across our full stack, make architectural decisions, work directly with customers to validate solutions, and ensure your systems scale as we grow.

  • Multiply the team's impact: write code that other engineers build on top of, establish patterns that improve our velocity, share knowledge that levels up the team, and help shape how we build at Opal.

Our Ideal Candidate Loves to:

  • Build end-to-end: you can take a customer problem, design the solution, and ship it across frontend and backend.

  • Think creatively: you're not a code monkey or a bot following specs. You question requirements, propose better approaches, and care about the "why" behind what you're building.

  • Thrive in undefined spaces: you get energized by ambiguous problems where there's no playbook. You'd rather figure out what to build than be handed a detailed spec.

  • Talk to customers: you want to understand who you're building for, what they need, and how Opal enables their growth and success

  • Explore a passion or curiosity in IAM / security

Benefits & Perks

  • Competitive Salary

  • Early employee equity

  • Top-tier Medical, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • Company and team bonding trips throughout the year fully covered by Opal Security

  • Daily lunch & coffee allowance

  • Unlimited PTO

  • 11 company holidays

  • One Medical Membership

  • 401k plan

  • Pre-Tax Commuter Benefits

This role is based in San Francisco. Remote optional

Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds rarely apply unless they meet all the job criteria. We aren’t looking for someone who ticks every single box on a page; we’re looking for lifelong learners and people who can make us better with their unique experiences. If you think you’d be a great fit, then please get in touch to tell us about yourself. Opal is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer.

  • Write technical reports and manuscripts in collaboration with NCATS project team and external investigators.
  • Write technical reports and prepare manuscripts in collaboration with investigators.
  • Deliver a minimum of one presentation per year to audiences outside the NIH.
  • Work products and documents related to developing and optimizing cell-based and
  • biochemical assays for fully automated robotic screening; evaluate new technologies for new screening strategies and novel assay formats; confirm assays and determine EC50/ specificity for primary active samples
  • Work products and documents related to maintaining and analyzing mammalian cell lines; maintain lab supplies and equipment; operate liquid dispensing systems and multimodal detectors/plate readers.
  • Work products and documents related to initiating and completing Chemical Probe Development Plans.
  • Work products and documents related to writing/preparing technical reports, manuscripts and oral presentations; work with staff on preparation of grant applications.

Job Details:

General Notes

As a top-10 engineering school with the No. 1 program in Texas, the Cockrell School of Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) has been a global leader in technology innovation and engineering education for over a century. With 11 undergraduate and 13 graduate programs, over 20 research centers and a faculty community that boasts one of the highest number of National Academy of Engineering members among U.S. universities, Texas Engineering has launched some of the nation’s most accomplished leaders and pioneered world-changing solutions in virtually every industry, from space exploration to energy to health care. Situated in the heart of Austin — named “America’s Coolest City” by Expedia and “The Best Place to Live in the U.S.” by U.S. News and World Report — the Cockrell School embodies the city’s innovative spirit. Major companies with Austin campuses, such as Dell, National Instruments, Apple, IBM, Samsung, Google and many others, continue to recruit Cockrell School students at a remarkable rate, launching thousands of successful careers and developing Texas Engineers into industry leaders.

ITG is the primary point of contact for technology support for the Dean’s groups within the Cockrell School of Engineering. ITG also supports several research groups.

Purpose

The Information Technology Coordinator II shares responsibility for sustaining the daily operations of Service Desk & Field Service. Responsible for desktop, laptop, printer and peripheral support. Devotes significant percentage of work schedule to providing technical support on Main campus; as well as at PRC and WPR locations.

Responsibilities

  • Effective handling of Service Desk phone support, web client requests, and in-person customer service requests while accurately notating requests in work order tools to provide professional, courteous, and precise communications to customers.

  • Daily hands-on troubleshooting/resolution support of WindowOS, MacOS, networking, printers, peripherals, software, and underlying infrastructure (via remote assistance or on-site).

  • Provide rapid front-line knowledgeable assistance in a variety of IT areas (Research Centers, Academic Departments, and Administrative Units to faculty, researchers, staff, and students).

  • Direct administration of systems, including setup, configuration, operation, network connectivity, VoIP, security and application installation, update, patching and licensing.

  • Help ensure compliance with all governing policy: Federal, State, UT System, Campus, School and funding agency requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • Knowledge of a broad spectrum of hardware, software, and networking IT components, from system administration to installation, operations, and troubleshooting with MS Windows, Apple, domains, directory and account services, application configuration, user accounts, security systems, protocol layering and much, much more.

  • Knowledge of active directory, imaging tools, and remote support tools.

  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.

  • Effective communications with both technical and non-technical employees.

  • Ability to work as part of a team and independently.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep networking expertise with ability to provide primary support for Engineering’s local area network and coordinate network planning, installations, upgrades and maintenance. Provide primary administration of subnets, VLANs, switches and DNS.

  • Articulate and collaborative with the ability to make things happen.

title: Adjunct Industrial Maintenance Instructor - Workforce & Skills Training
description:
Position Summary
Adjunct Instructor positions are temporary, part-time positions hired on an as-needed basis to support workforce and
skills training initiatives. The Adjunct Industrial Maintenance Instructor will create a hands-on learning environment that
supports adult learners in developing practical maintenance, troubleshooting, and technical skills aligned with modern
manufacturing and industry needs.
This role focuses on delivering non-credit industrial maintenance training for workforce development. Training may range
from foundational maintenance skills to advanced technical topics based on instructor expertise and employer needs.
Instructors may teach at Ivy Tech Community College - Richmond or onsite at employer locations throughout the
surrounding service area. Applicants are not required to have expertise in every industrial maintenance discipline.
Instructors may be selected to teach courses within their specific area(s) of professional expertise.

Major Responsibilities

• Deliver high-quality, hands-on industrial maintenance training in classroom, lab, and employer-site settings.

• Facilitate adult learning through demonstrations, equipment exercises, troubleshooting scenarios, and practical applications.

• Provide or assist with course outlines, instructional materials, lab activities, and assessments aligned with workforce training objectives.

• Adapt instruction to participants with varying levels of industrial experience and technical knowledge.

• Maintain accurate attendance, progress, assessment, and course-completion records.

• Submit required course documentation within established timelines.

• Support participants with questions and technical skill development throughout training.

• Address participant concerns and collaborate with Ivy Tech Workforce/Skills Training staff as needed.

• Meet all scheduled training sessions as assigned.

• Utilize instructional technologies such as PowerPoint, Canvas, simulation software, or manufacturer-specific training platforms when appropriate.

• Promote a professional, respectful, inclusive, and safety-focused learning environment.

• Ensure the safe use of tools, equipment, trainers, and laboratory resources. Industrial Maintenance Training Areas Qualified instructors may teach in one or more of the following areas based on their experience and expertise:

• Industrial Maintenance Fundamentals

• Preventive and Predictive Maintenance

• Mechanical Systems and Troubleshooting

• Industrial Electrical Fundamentals

• Electrical Troubleshooting

• Motors, Motor Controls, and Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)

• Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs)

• Siemens and/or Allen-Bradley PLC Systems • Industrial Robotics • FANUC Robot Operations and Programming

• Hydraulics and Pneumatics • Pumps, Bearings, Belts, Chains, and Power Transmission Systems

• Industrial Troubleshooting and Root Cause Analysis

• Industrial Safety and Lockout/Tagout

• Mechatronics and Automated Manufacturing Systems

• Other industrial maintenance and advanced manufacturing topics based on employer needs Instructors may also assist in developing or customizing short-term training for employer partners based on specific equipment, processes, or workforce skill gaps

Minimum Qualifications

• Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant hands-on industrial maintenance, manufacturing, automation, electrical, mechanical, robotics, or related technical experience.

• Demonstrated expertise in at least one industrial maintenance or advanced manufacturing discipline.

• Strong understanding of applicable industrial safety practices.

• Ability to explain technical concepts clearly and translate industry experience into practical, hands-on instruction.

• Ability to effectively work with adult learners with varying levels of experience.

• Ability to demonstrate proper troubleshooting, maintenance, and/or equipment-operation techniques within the instructor's area of expertise. • High school diploma or equivalent with substantial relevant industry experience required. Preferred Qualifications

• Associate's degree or higher in Industrial Technology, Advanced Manufacturing, Electrical Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering Technology, Mechatronics, Automation, or a related field.

• Previous experience as an industrial maintenance technician, maintenance supervisor, controls technician, automation technician, engineer, skilled tradesperson, or similar role.

• Prior teaching, technical training, apprenticeship, mentoring, or workforce-development experience.

• Manufacturer-specific training or certifications related to PLCs, robotics, automation, electrical systems, mechanical systems, or industrial equipment.

• Industry-recognized credentials such as OSHA, NFPA 70E, NCCER, MSSC, SACA, FANUC, Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Siemens, or other relevant credentials.

• Experience developing or delivering customized employer-based technical training.

• Experience troubleshooting industrial equipment in a manufacturing environment.

Work Environment

This is a part-time, as-needed adjunct position. Training schedules vary based on employer and program needs and may include daytime, evening, or occasional weekend instruction. A significant portion of workforce training may occur during normal daytime business hours, particularly when training employees for local manufacturing partners. Instruction may take place at Ivy Tech Community College - Richmond or onsite at employer facilities. Local travel may be required. Course assignments will be based on the instructor's qualifications, technical expertise, availability, and employer training needs.

About the Opportunity

This position is well suited for experienced maintenance technicians, skilled trades professionals, engineers, automation specialists, retirees, and other industry professionals interested in sharing their knowledge with the next generation of manufacturing and maintenance professionals. Adjunct instructors can help Ivy Tech respond to the technical workforce needs of area employers while continuing to remain active in their field on a flexible, part-time basis.

Part-Time Employee Benefits Health & Wellness

• Employee Assistance Program offering no-cost confidential counseling sessions, legal consultations, financial planning consultations, and other resources. Financial & Retirement Benefits

• Employees may contribute pre-tax or post-tax dollars through payroll deduction to build retirement savings. Educational Benefits

• Fee remission opportunities for eligible employees, spouses, and legal dependents. Additional eligibility requirements and benefit provisions are subject to Ivy Tech Community College policies

Ivy Tech is committed to supporting the well-being, growth, and financial security of our part-time employees. These benefits include:

Health & Wellness

  • Access to a comprehensive vision care plan with low-cost exams and allowances for glasses or contact lenses

  • Employee Assistance Program offering no cost confidential counseling sessions, legal consultations, financial planning consultations, and other resources

Financial & Retirement Benefits

  • All employees can contribute pre-tax or post-tax dollars through payroll deduction to build retirement savings

Educational Benefits

  • Fee remission for employees, spouses, and legal dependents.

For more information on Ivy Tech Benefits, visit .


Ivy Tech Community College is an accredited, equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, marital status, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age or veteran status. As required by Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, Ivy Tech Community College does not discriminate on the basis of sex, including sexual harassment in its educational programs and activities, including employment and admissions. Questions specific to Title IX may be referred to the College’s Title IX Coordinator or to the US Department of Education Office of Civil Rights.

title: Assistive Technology Specialist (3457)
description:
Access Technology Coordinator (Part-Time, Flexible Schedule – 10 Hours/Week)

Help transform lives through technology! Join MAB Community Services and empower individuals who are blind or visually impaired to gain independence, confidence, and access to the digital world.

MAB Community Services is a non-profit human service organization dedicated to supporting individuals with disabilities, including adults with developmental disabilities, adults with acquired brain injuries, individuals who are blind or visually impaired, and adolescents with autism. We are seeking an enthusiastic and innovative Access Technology Coordinator to join our team and help individuals maximize their independence through assistive technology.

This part-time position (10 hours per week with a flexible schedule) provides meaningful hands-on support by assessing technology needs, providing training, troubleshooting devices, and helping individuals build the skills needed to navigate today’s digital world.

Under the direction of the Director of Access Technology Training, the Access Technology Coordinator will support the operation and growth of MAB’s Access Technology Program throughout Boston and surrounding communities.

What You’ll Do:

  • Conduct assistive technology assessments, training, coaching, and ongoing support for individuals who are blind or visually impaired.

  • Teach clients how to use access technology tools, including screen readers, magnification software, mobile accessibility features, and other adaptive technologies.

  • Provide technical troubleshooting and support for assistive technology devices and software.

  • Develop and deliver individualized lessons, trainings, and educational programs.

  • Support and coordinate volunteer technology instructors, including training and scheduling.

  • Maintain accurate participant records and documentation while following HIPAA confidentiality standards.

  • Build relationships with community partners, senior centers, healthcare providers, and local organizations.

  • Participate in outreach activities and presentations to increase awareness of access technology services.

  • Research and stay current on emerging assistive technologies and accessibility practices.

  • Support technology pilots, user testing, and program development initiatives.

  • Provide training and consultation to MABVI staff, including Occupational Therapists and Orientation & Mobility specialists, as needed.

Why Join MAB?

Make a Meaningful Impact – Your work will directly help individuals gain greater independence and access to education, employment, and community resources.

Flexible Schedule – Enjoy a part-time schedule designed to provide meaningful work with flexibility.

Innovative Work Environment – Be part of a program focused on advancing accessibility and using technology to remove barriers.

Professional Growth – Expand your expertise in assistive technology, accessibility, disability services, and community-based programming.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred in technology, education, rehabilitation, disability studies, or related field; equivalent experience considered.

  • Experience working with individuals who are blind or visually impaired, individuals with disabilities, or within rehabilitation services strongly preferred.

  • Knowledge of assistive technology including screen readers, magnification tools, Braille technology, and accessibility software.

  • Familiarity with Windows, Mac, Android, and iOS operating systems.

  • Knowledge of digital accessibility standards and best practices, including WCAG and ADA accessibility principles preferred.

  • Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to maintain confidential records and manage participant information.

  • Experience developing training materials, curriculum, or technology instruction preferred.

  • Certifications such as CATIS, CPACC, or similar accessibility/assistive technology credentials preferred.

Ready to use technology to create opportunities and independence? Apply today and become part of the MAB Community Services team!

title: Financial Coach
description:
Join Our Team as a Financial Coach

We are seeking a Financial Coach to join our Center for Working Families (CWF) team. In this role, you will provide one-on-one financial counseling and group workshops for low- to moderate-income individuals. You’ll support clients in building credit, managing debt, saving for the future, and accessing financial resources. This is a great opportunity for someone passionate about financial empowerment and community impact.

A Day in the Life:

As a Financial Coach, your day begins by meeting one-on-one with clients—individuals and families seeking support to improve their financial well-being. You’ll listen closely, assess their needs, and help them create personalized action plans for budgeting, saving, debt reduction, and credit building. Between sessions, you might prepare for an upcoming workshop on topics like smart banking or identity theft protection, tailoring content to the audience's needs. You’ll collaborate with colleagues in team meetings to ensure clients are accessing the full range of support available through the Center for Working Families. Throughout the day, you’ll update client records, track progress toward program goals, and coordinate with community partners or financial institutions to connect clients with helpful products or services. Your role is dynamic, people-centered, and deeply impactful—each day presents new opportunities to empower others and help them take control of their financial futures.

Schedule:

  • Standard 40-hour workweek
  • Some evenings (until 6:30-7 PM) and early mornings may be required
  • Team members rotate evening shifts for job training support (Tues & Thurs coverage)

You Would Thrive in this Position If:

  • 2+ years of experience in financial coaching, credit counseling, or a related field preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, or a related area preferred. Equivalent experience considered (minimum 4 years).
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and motivational skills.
  • Experience in teaching or leading workshops is a plus.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and comfortable using data management systems.
  • Knowledge of challenges faced by low-income communities and available support resources.
  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail and time management skills.

Join us and use your expertise to make a tangible difference in the lives of families striving for financial success. Your innovative approach and dedication will help drive our mission forward. Apply today to be a part of a team that's committed to empowering our community, one family at a time.

title: Customer Supply Chain Planner Specialist
description:
Introduction

ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our main headquarters are located in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.

ASML has an industry-leading supply-chain management (SCM) organization, responsible for ensuring material availability to ASML’s factories and customers. Our DNA contains customer focus, concurrent engineering, virtual integration plus the ability to thrive in a volatile market, accelerate the supply chain and deliver creative solutions. SCM plans up to four years ahead while customer requirements and system bill of materials can change at any time. Any break in material availability can have an unacceptable impact for our customers. So SCM must proactively identify and solve potential issues by working closely with our technical departments and customers, and actively managing an extensive supplier base.

Role and Responsibilities

The Customer Supply Chain Planner Specialist manages assigned customer supply chain operations within the United States. This role is responsible for managing assigned site performance and day-to-day operations, while building relationships with internal stakeholders and external customers to meet and align on expectations.

Responsibilities related to:

  • Performance Management:

    • Responsible for assigned site supply chain performance, including:

    • Ensure service contract commitments and targets are met.

    • Maintain and improve cooperation between local, regional, and central supply chain teams to support optimal execution.

    • Secure relevant performance reporting for stakeholders.

  • Demand, Planning and Analysis:

    • Responsible for inputting correct demand into the system.

    • Act as the key contact for the Regional Planning team, FMA, and Service Management organizations to ensure effective planning and material availability, including critical material management.

    • Monitor critical materials and ensure effective site coverage.

  • Customer Intimacy:

    • Manage and improve internal and external customer relationships, communication, and performance on a day-to-day basis. Meet with stakeholders, provide reports, and support continuous improvement efforts.

  • Cost Management:

    • Assist in support of site P&L.

    • Deliver on assigned cost targets.

    • Support cost reduction programs.

  • Process and Development:

    • Support personal development toward job requirements.

    • Drive process standardization and efficiencies via LEAN.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required; focus in Business Management, Logistics, or Supply Chain preferred.

  • 3–5 years of relevant experience in a complex, customer-oriented environment managing multiple priorities.

  • In-depth knowledge of SAP or a similar ERP system.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, specifically Excel and PowerPoint.

  • Knowledge of business complexity, supply chain, and/or relevant industry experience strongly preferred.

  • Experience implementing new processes across the supply chain against agreed costs preferred.

  • Knowledge of ASML supply chain procedures preferred.

Personal Skills

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:

  • Analytical, with the ability to organize and prioritize workload.

  • Leadership skills, drive for results, and the ability to perform under high pressure and tight timelines.

  • Excellent social and communication (both written and verbal) skills.

  • Service-minded and customer-focused.

  • Strong data analysis and problem-solving abilities.

  • Results-oriented team player with a proactive attitude, “can-do” mentality, flexibility, and a high level of commitment.

  • Remain flexible in providing after-hours support, as needed.

Other Information

  • Must be willing to be available occasionally on weekends for escalation management.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch.

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the campus.

  • The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.

  • May require travel, depending on company needs.

  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

  • Ability to work under deadlines.

  • The work environment is generally moderate in temperature and noise level.

  • Must be able to read and interpret data, information, and documents.

  • Ability to observe and respond to people and situations and interact with others encountered during the course of work.

  • Ability to learn and apply new information or skills.

You must be work authorized in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship.

$63,200-86,900

Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members.

The Company offers employees and their families, medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. Job Code: 44643

Job Location: Camden, NJ (on-site)

Job Schedule: 9/80 (Employees work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked – and have every other Friday off)

Job Description:

In a fast moving and increasingly complex world, L3Harris is anticipating and rapidly responding to challenges with agile technology – creating a safer and more secure future. Join our trailblazing team, where you'll dive into the thrilling world of high-assurance encryption products.

L3Harris Integrated Systems & Encryption division is seeking a Software Engineer. Responsibilities include the translation of requirements into working and maintainable solutions for our Encryption business. The selected candidate will apply technical proficiency across various stages of our software development life cycle, gather requirements, and work closely with stakeholders to prioritize and scope tasks. The selected candidate will be working as a key team member on a Scrum team and will be instrumental in setting our direction and strategy for product and infrastructure development.

Essential Functions:

  • Investigate root cause of complex issues, and implement solutions, working independently or with a multi-discipline team.
  • Apply computer science, engineering, and mathematical analysis concepts and principles in the development of software for the target hardware.
  • Work closely with cross functional members of the engineering organization to develop and evaluate interfaces between hardware and software, and operational performance requirements and design of the overall system.
  • Support and participate in all phases of the software development life cycle, including requirements analysis, design, implementation, hardware-software integration, and formal test.
  • Develop software test plans and procedures, and other relevant technical documentation.
  • Utilize modeling tools and equipment to establish operating data, conduct experimental tests, prototype, and evaluate results.
  • Participate in peer reviews, identify, track and repair defects.
  • Utilize a variety of software languages (primarily C/C++, Rust, and Python), implementing software for embedded real time operating systems.
  • Lead small project efforts or investigations.
  • Ability to travel about 10%.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret security clearance.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 6 years of prior relevant experience.
  • 1+ years of experience developing Rust software for production systems.
  • At least 2 years of experience with software design and development experience using C/C++ programming languages and object-oriented design.

Preferred Additional Skills:

  • Master’s degree highly preferred.
  • Active security clearance is highly preferred.

title: Software Development Test Engineer
description:
Everforth ECS is seeking a Software Development Test Engineer to work in a Arlington, VA (Hybrid) .

About the Role

ECS seeks a dynamic and experienced Software Development Test Engineer to ensure the quality, reliability, and security of a large-scale, public-facing web platform serving enterprise clients managing critical digital infrastructure. You'll work embedded within an agile development team, collaborating closely with developers, team leads, UX/UI designers, and product stakeholders to deliver accessible, secure, and high-quality solutions. This platform includes complex features such as multi-entity account management, infrastructure services provisioning, secure administrative workflows, and domain management capabilities. A strong desire and aptitude for learning is essential-our solution is rapidly evolving with new requirements, technologies, and an ever-changing threat landscape. The ideal candidate will bring both manual and automated testing expertise, a passion for quality advocacy, and the ability to think holistically about system reliability across the full stack.

Job Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and execute comprehensive test strategies including manual and automated testing to validate functionality, performance, security, and accessibility across the full stack (frontend UI, backend APIs, database operations, domain registry/DNS operations, and complex end-to-end workflows).
  • Build and maintain automated testing frameworks, integrate testing into CI/CD pipelines, and proactively recommend improvements to increase automation coverage and testing efficiency.
  • Ensure compliance with federal accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA / Section 508) and security requirements (Federal ATO, Login.gov/OIDC authentication), incorporating automated accessibility and security testing into development workflows.
  • Identify, document, track, and verify resolution of defects using issue tracking systems; maintain test documentation and provide clear reporting on testing progress, coverage, and quality metrics.
  • Collaborate with developers, the Technical Team Lead, product managers, and UX/UI designers throughout the agile development lifecycle-participating in sprint ceremonies, code reviews, and requirements discussions while serving as a quality advocate and identifying testability concerns early.
  • Continuously evaluate and recommend testing tools, methodologies, and process improvements that enhance team effectiveness and align with modern web application best practices.

Salary Range: $140,000 - $160,000

General Description of Benefits

  • Must be a US Citizen
  • Must be able to obtain a Public Trust Clearance
  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related technical discipline
  • 5+ years of experience in software quality assurance and testing, with a mix of manual and automated testing
  • 5+ years of hands‑on experience testing enterprise‑scale web applications built with modern web technologies (Python/Django and JavaScript frameworks)
  • 5+ years of experience developing and maintaining automated test frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, pytest, or similar)
  • Experience testing full stack web applications including frontend UI, backend APIs and database interactions
  • Experience with testing in Agile/Scrum environments and integrating testing into SecDevOps/CI/CD pipelines
  • Working knowledge of Git-based version control and pull‑request workflows
  • Experience with issue-tracking and test management tools (Jira, TestRail, GitHub, or similar)
  • Experience with accessibility testing to meet WCAG 2.1 AA / Section 508 standards, including use of automated accessibility testing tools
  • Experience testing applications that must meet federal security requirements and compliance standards
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience with testing cloud‑deployed, containerized applications
  • Experience testing relational database operations and API integrations
