The Team

The Actions team sits at the heart of Staffbase's AI ambitions. We're the team that gives Navigator — our AI assistant and the main entry point into Staffbase — the ability to actually do things: submit a form, complete a task inside an integration, or take an action on a user's behalf through the agent. If Navigator is the brain, we build the hands.

That means two big things. First, we enrich what the AI can see and act on, our plugins, our widgets and the wider Staffbase platform so the assistant can do real work, not just talk about it. Second, we build the extensions that connect to the tools people already use, like Workday, Personio, ServiceNow and Microsoft.   We're not just shipping features, though. A core part of our mission is building the extensibility framework that lets others build too.  

What you'll be doing

  • Building a UI component library that generated apps can assemble from, turning components like payslip views and approval flows into maintained, reusable pieces instead of regenerated artifacts
  • Creating the connection layer between generated apps and customer source systems—HR platforms, time-tracking and scheduling systems, and a long tail of vendors with thin or undocumented APIs
  • Defining extension points (widgets, menus, sidebars) so plugins declare where they surface and what they connect to in a single, clean configuration
  • Designing and implementing a cross-integration authentication solution that lets customers run multiple integrations without forcing employees to log in repeatedly
  • Shipping plugins on the platform yourself, staying a consumer of what we build so we catch gaps early

What you need to be successful

  • Strong knowledge of React and TypeScript for frontend work Java/Kotlin or Go an TypeScript experience for backend services
  • Real experience integrating third-party APIs, especially the challenging ones—inconsistent auth, partial documentation, legacy and on-prem systems
  • Deep understanding of multi-tenancy security and data isolation; you care about scope checks and preventing cross-tenant leaks
  • Good judgment about what to standardize and what to leave flexible—drawing that line in the right place is central to this role

Nice to have experience 

  • You are comfortable with edge and serverless runtimes like Cloudflare Workers
  • You have built a plugin system, SDK, or developer platform before
  • Developed a design system or component library that other teams depended on
  • Real-world experience with OAuth and enterprise SSO
  • Experience treating AI code generation as a product surface, not just a personal tool

What you'll get

  • Competitive Compensation - we offer attractive salary packages including LTIP (unit-based Long Term Incentive Plan)
  • Flexibility - we offer flexible working time models and the option of hybrid work, and support this with a yearly flex work allowance of €1560
  • Recharge - with 31 vacation days annually (incl. one floating holiday), plus pro rata fully paid Fridays off during August
  • Support - we offer offering a company pension scheme
  • Volunteers Day - you’ll get one day off per year for supporting a social project

title: Career Counselor (3458)
description:
Who We Are

At MAB Community Services, we are dedicated to empowering individuals with acquired or traumatic brain injuries to achieve meaningful employment and community involvement. We believe in fostering independence and enhancing quality of life through tailored support and resources.

The Ivy Street School is a small year-round private residential special education school committed to advancing equity and access for young people living with disabilities. We serve neurodiverse adolescents ages 13-22. We support the whole child through a student-first model that is driven by collaboration, a willingness to think big, and a commitment to knowing our students well.

We believe that every student is exceptional, and at Ivy Street, we work tirelessly to create the educational and therapeutic conditions for our students to thrive. As a community, we are focused on the immediate needs of our scholars with an unwavering eye on their future needs and the concrete plans to achieve them. Our multidisciplinary team works to create rich and meaningful experiences that will nurture learning and prepare our students for their transition into adulthood and independent living. While our classrooms have four walls, we consider Boston our second classroom, and our students are often making meaning and deepening learning throughout the city.

The Position

We are seeking a Career Counselor to join our team. The Career Counselor, under the supervision of the Director of Career Development, prepares students for employment using a person-centered approach. We prioritize individual goals and strive to promote self-determination and advocacy throughout the span of employment. Students learn by doing, in a variety of hands-on employment opportunities that promote success and meet them where they are at. Where each student starts depends on their age, experience, and goals. Career Counselors use a model of fading support that connects students to the resources they need while working towards greater independence. Career Counselors provide direct career services to a caseload of students, lead career development blocks in classrooms, and support students in campus and community-based opportunities.

Supervision, support, and professional learning are provided. Ivy Street School is driven by trauma-informed care, and we use Positive Behavior Interventions and Supports and Restorative Justice to support positive behavior development and deepen character. Our organization is committed to deepening its work in anti-racism and seeks team members who are committed to that fight.
Key Responsibilities
  • Carrying a caseload of students by providing direct career services and being a part of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Conducting screenings of employment aged students to identify strengths, areas of growth, and need for career services.
  • Providing supervision, job coaching and coordination of on-grounds and community-based student employment to support skill development.
  • Transporting students to and from employment opportunities by driving, utilizing public transportation or via ridesharing services.
  • Participating in the IEP process by assessing needs and writing goals, attending IEP meetings, providing services that address IEP goals, documenting progress, and conducting vocational evaluations.
  • Collaborating with interdisciplinary team through monthly team meetings and weekly collaborations.
  • Participating in planning for employment component of students transition to post-secondary adult living.
  • Completing paperwork by deadlines including weekly documentation, IEP goals, IEP progress reports, progress reports for state agency treatment plans, etc.
  • Attending weekly collaboration meetings for all individuals on their caseload to address employment needs/concerns
  • Initiating and maintaining parent contact, as needed, for each student on their caseload

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Experience working with youth in an educational setting preferred
  • A valid driver’s license
  • CPI, CPR and First Aid certifications required (offered upon hire)
  • A background check, drug/alcohol test and TB testing to be conducting prior to start

Job Type: Full time in person

Schedule: Monday-Friday 10:30-4:30pm

Location: Ivy Street School

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 403(b), generous earned time package and more!

Join us at Ivy Street School for the opportunity to work, learn, and grow alongside an expert multidisciplinary team and make a lasting impact in the lives of young people with disabilities!

description:
Job title: Associate Director Managed Care Operations

Location: Morristown, NJ


About the Job

The Associate Director of Managed Care Operations is a key operational role responsible for supporting and advancing the operational, regulatory, and technological functions within Managed Care Operations. This position plays an important role in helping ensure the organization's compliance with federal programs, driving process improvements, and contributing to high-priority strategic initiatives that impact financial performance and operational efficiency.

The Associate Director will serve as a lead contributor for the CMS Maximum Fair Price (MFP) initiative—a high-visibility federal program spanning design through execution—supporting the development of internal process architecture, helping define business requirements, and taking ownership of day-to-day operations post-launch. Additionally, this role includes designing and implementing an end-to-end process for managed care invoice prefunding with Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs), helping establish this function and serving as a subject matter expert for prefunding workflows and financial controls.

The Associate Director will help advance the application of Artificial Intelligence to drive operational efficiency within Managed Care Operations, supporting the development of AI-powered solutions for formulary validation and identifying opportunities to enhance invoice processing workflows. This role involves assessing emerging technologies, contributing to business cases for AI adoption, and partnering with IT and Data Science teams to help translate innovative concepts into measurable business value.

Beyond these core initiatives, the Associate Director will support the migration to the new Validata platform, manage processing and reporting for all four CMS Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) programs, and play a role in developing team talent and supporting operational continuity across the function.

A strong cross-functional collaborator, the Associate Director will work closely with Treasury, Finance, Legal, Strategic Pricing, Government Pricing, Digital, Contract Development, and Account Management teams to align on priorities and deliver measurable results. Success in this role requires solid managed care industry expertise, strong analytical and regulatory acumen, excellent organizational skills, and the ability to manage through change in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and Specialty Care neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About Sanofi

We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities

  • Shape MFP internal process architecture, define business requirements, and manage day-to-day program operations post-launch. Coordinate daily payment processing with third-party vendors and ensure ongoing compliance and financial accuracy.

  • Design and implement an end-to-end PBM prefunding process with Pharmacy Benefit Managers, including frameworks for tracking, monitoring, and resolving funding discrepancies. Coordinate with Treasury, Finance, Account Management, and Operations on funding strategies while serving as primary subject matter expert and process lead.

  • Drive tactical implementation of AI to enhance operational efficiency within Managed Care Operations, including developing AI-powered solutions for formulary validation and improving invoice processing workflows. Assess emerging technologies, contribute to business cases for adoption, and collaborate with IT and Data Science teams to translate innovations into measurable business value.

  • Own end-to-end processing and reporting for all four CMS IRA programs while ensuring strict adherence to regulatory deadlines to avoid penalties and regulatory risk. Partner with Finance, Strategic Pricing, and Government Pricing to manage multiple concurrent compliance deadlines with precision.

  • Serve as primary business liaison for the transition from the legacy ECP system to the Validata platform, supporting requirements definition, testing, and workflow integration. Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs to minimize operational disruption.

  • Support SOX control compliance for Managed Care Operations, ensuring adherence to all control requirements and maintaining accurate documentation. Coordinate with internal audit activities conducted by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), serving as a key point of contact for audit inquiries, evidence requests, and remediation efforts.

  • Process and manage invoices from managed care customers outside the Big 3 customer base, ensuring accurate tracking, timely payment processing, and compliance with contract terms. Coordinate with Account Management and Finance to resolve discrepancies and maintain strong vendor relationships.

  • Train, mentor, and provide backup coverage for team members during extended absences and vacancies while maintaining cross-functional knowledge to ensure uninterrupted service delivery.

  • Partner with Treasury, Legal, Finance, Pricing & Analytics, Digital, Contract Development, and Account Management as a subject matter expert across multiple managed care disciplines.

  • Support Director, Managed Care Operations on ad hoc projects as required.

About You

  • 4 years of Model N experience

  • Ability to take ownership of initiatives and drive them to completion

  • Strong project management skills

  • Financial experience preferred

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with external vendors

  • Strong oral and written communications skills

  • Collaborative mindset, consistently fostering teamwork to achieve shared goals and drive organizational success

  • Highly organized, meticulous, and detail-oriented, with a disciplined approach and unwavering commitment to delivering superior quality work

Why Choose Us?

  • Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether it’s through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally.

title: Director of Project Controls
description:
Job Summary

The Director of Project and Document Controls serves as the central authority for project documentation governance, project controls oversight, and PMIS optimization across assigned project portfolios. This role provides dedicated, high‑integrity, administrative, technical, and audit-ready support to Project Management teams, ensuring all project information is accurate, current, compliant, and readily accessible from initiation through closeout.

By leading the project documentation audit function, the Director ensures that all project records submittals, RFIs, test reports, commissioning documents, schedules, budgets, and change logs adhere to contractual, regulatory, and CBRE Government & Defense standards. The role acts as the critical link between project teams and leadership by maintaining reliable information flows, enabling proactive decision-making, and preventing schedule disruptions caused by documentation gaps.

Primary Job Functions - Project Controls & Governance

  • Establish, implement, and continuously improve project controls processes aligned with contractual requirements, federal regulations, USACE/NAVFAC quality standards, and CBRE governance.

  • Oversee schedule updates, critical-path impacts, and milestone tracking to maintain schedule integrity and minimize delays.

  • Coordinate with Project Managers to ensure compliance with Beneficial Occupancy, Substantial Completion, commissioning, testing, and closeout requirements.

Document Control Leadership

  • Manage the full document lifecycle, including intake, indexing, review, approval routing, archiving, and controlled distribution.

  • Manage submittals and RFIs, coordinating with government stakeholders to support timely resolution and schedule progress.

PMIS Administration & Optimization

Audit Readiness & Compliance

Project Communication & Reporting

title: Facilities Supervisor
description:
Who we are:

At Vireo Health, we’re not just another cannabis company—we’re a movement. Founded by physicians and driven by innovation, we blend science, technology, and passion to create top-tier cannabis products and experiences. Our team of 500+ bold creators and trailblazers are shaping the future of the industry, and we want you to be part of it.

We take pride in being one of the most diverse and inclusive workplaces in cannabis, fostering a culture where everyone belongs. Through employee engagement, community events, and non-profit partnerships, we’re building more than a business—we’re building a community.

As we rapidly expand nationwide, we’re looking for talented, driven, and passionate people to join us. If you’re ready to turn your passion into a career, let’s grow the future together.

What we offer:

  • Compensation: $60,000-65,000 annually
  • Competitive health, dental, and vision insurance on the 1st of the month after you start
  • 401k and life insurance
  • 11 days of accrued PTO in addition to 2 wellness days and volunteer hours

What the role is about:

This position oversees facilities operations across both the Hurlock and Massey locations. Travel between sites will be required based on operational needs.

What impact you'll make:

  • Provide leadership and direct supervision to facilities technicians at both locations, including coaching, training, scheduling, and performance management

  • Manage day-to-day facilities operations to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable functionality of both sites

  • Conduct routine inspections of premises, equipment, and systems to identify maintenance needs and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards

  • Perform and/or oversee basic repairs and maintenance of facility systems, including:

  • Plumbing (pipes, pumps, fixtures)

  • Electrical (lighting, minor wiring needs)

  • HVAC systems

  • Minor structural repairs

  • Repair or coordinate repairs of facility mechanical processing equipment, including vendor management when specialized service is required.

  • Develop, implement, and monitor preventative maintenance plans for both locations

  • Establish, manage, and monitor waste service providers and related compliance

  • Submit, track, and manage facilities maintenance tickets through the company’s maintenance system

  • Maintain and manage inventories of spare parts, tools, and equipment to support continuous facility functionality

  • Partner with Directors to prepare repair estimates, support capital projects, and assist in developing facility improvement budgets

  • Coordinate subcontractor work and ensure all facilities improvements meet quality, safety, and timeline requirements

  • Collaborate with Corporate Real Estate to plan and execute larger facility improvement projects

  • Ensure adherence to sanitation practices, facility cleanliness, and safety procedures, including routine cleaning tasks (sweeping, mopping, garbage removal, vacuuming, etc.)

  • Participate in weekly team meetings and provide regular updates to leadership on facility operations, challenges, and progress

  • Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement within the facilities team

  • Act as a point of escalation for urgent facility issues and coordinate appropriate response

  • All other duties as assigned by the Directors or Corporate Facilities Manager to ensure smooth and efficient facility operations

What you've accomplished:

  • Proven Maintenance Experience

  • Skilled in the use of power tools

  • Ability to use common tools such as hammers, hoists, saws, drills, and wrenches

  • Ability to take apart machines, equipment, or devices to remove and replace defective parts

  • Ability to check blueprints, repair manuals, or parts catalogs as necessary

  • Ability to work flexible schedule, including off business hours as needed

  • Must be at least 21 years of age

  • Must have a valid driver's license

Physical Demands

Ability to communicate orally with management and other co-workers is crucial. Regular use of the telephone and e-mail for communication may be required. Standing for extended periods is common. Hearing and vision within normal ranges is essential for normal conversations, to receive ordinary information and to prepare or inspect equipment. Some heavy lifting may be required. Exertion of up to 50 lbs. of force occasionally may be required.

Work Environment

The job is performed indoors and outdoors. Must be able to work in hot, humid environments for extended periods of time with exposure to dust, allergens, and water. Appropriate PPE will be provided. Activities include extended periods of sitting, standing, kneeling, stooping and bending. Twisting in tight areas may also be required at times.

Why Choose Vireo?

Life’s too short to work somewhere that doesn’t ignite your passion. The cannabis industry is fast-paced, innovative, and full of opportunity—where science meets creativity, and wellness meets culture.

At Vireo Health, we’re pioneering the future of cannabis with a team that’s as dynamic as the industry itself. Here, you’ll find a workplace that’s collaborative, inclusive, and driven by HEART and purpose, where your work has a real impact on people’s lives.

Whether you’re cultivating the highest-quality plants, crafting cutting-edge products, or shaping unforgettable customer experiences, you’ll be part of something bigger. If you’re looking for a career that’s exciting, meaningful, and full of growth, let’s build the future of cannabis together.

✅ A Growing Industry: Work at the leading tech company in the cannabis industry and help shape the future

✅ Passionate Culture: Join a team that truly cares about the plant, the people, and the purpose behind what we do
✅ Employee Perks: Enjoy competitive pay and benefits, paid time off and employee discounts

✅ Making an Impact: We’re committed to education, sustainability, and giving back to the communities we serve.

EEO Statement

title: Adjunct CNC Machining & Programming Instructor Workforce & Skills Training
description:
Position Summary
Adjunct Instructor positions are temporary, part-time positions hired on an as-needed basis to support workforce and
skills training initiatives. The Adjunct CNC Machining & Programming Instructor will create a hands-on learning
environment that supports adult learners in developing practical machining, CNC operation, setup, programming, and
troubleshooting skills aligned with modern manufacturing needs.
This role focuses on delivering non-credit CNC machining and programming training for workforce development. Training
may range from introductory machining and CNC operation to advanced setup and programming based on instructor
expertise and employer needs.
Instructors may teach at Ivy Tech Community College - Richmond or onsite at employer locations throughout the
surrounding service area. Applicants are not required to have expertise in every CNC machine, controller, or
programming platform. Instructors may be selected to teach courses within their specific area(s) of professional
expertise.

Major Responsibilities

Deliver high-quality, hands-on CNC machining and programming training in classroom, lab, and employer-site settings.

• Facilitate adult learning through machine demonstrations, setup exercises, programming activities, troubleshooting scenarios, and practical applications.

• Provide or assist with course outlines, instructional materials, lab activities, and assessments aligned with workforce training objectives.

• Demonstrate safe and proper operation of CNC machines, tooling, workholding devices, and related equipment.

• Adapt instruction to participants with varying levels of machining and manufacturing experience.

• Maintain accurate attendance, progress, assessment, and course-completion records.

• Submit required course documentation within established timelines.

• Support participants with technical questions and skill development throughout training.

• Address participant concerns and collaborate with Ivy Tech Workforce/Skills Training staff as needed.

• Meet all scheduled training sessions as assigned.

• Utilize instructional technologies such as PowerPoint, Canvas, CNC simulation software, CAD/CAM software, or manufacturer-specific programming platforms when appropriate.

• Promote a professional, respectful, inclusive, and safety-focused learning environment.

• Ensure the safe use of machines, tooling, measuring equipment, and laboratory resources

CNC Machining & Programming Training Areas Qualified instructors may teach in one or more of the following areas based on their experience and expertise:

• CNC Machining Fundamentals

• CNC Machine Operation • CNC Mill Setup and Operation

• CNC Lathe Setup and Operation

• CNC Programming

• G-Code and M-Code Programming

• Conversational Programming

• CNC Setup, Tooling, and Workholding

• Machine Offsets and Tool Compensation

• Blueprint Reading

• Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T;)

• Precision Measurement and Inspection

• Machining Math

• Cutting Tools, Speeds, and Feeds

• Manual Machining Fundamentals

• CNC Troubleshooting • Process Improvement and Cycle-Time Optimization

• CAD/CAM Programming

• Mastercam or other CAM software

• FANUC CNC Controls

• Haas CNC Controls

• Other CNC machining, programming, and advanced manufacturing topics based on employer needs Instructors may also assist in developing or customizing short-term CNC training for employer partners based on specific machines, controllers, software, manufacturing processes, or workforce skill gaps

Minimum Qualifications

• Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant hands-on CNC machining, CNC programming, tool and die, manufacturing, or related technical experience.

• Demonstrated expertise in at least one CNC machining or programming discipline.

• Working knowledge of CNC machine operation, setup, tooling, machining processes, and applicable safety practices.

• Ability to explain technical machining concepts clearly and translate industry experience into practical, hands-on instruction.

• Ability to effectively work with adult learners with varying levels of machining experience.

• Ability to demonstrate proper machine setup, operation, programming, inspection, and/or troubleshooting techniques within the instructor's area of expertise.

• High school diploma or equivalent with substantial relevant industry experience required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Associate's degree or higher in Machine Tool Technology, Advanced Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering Technology, CNC Technology, or a related field.

• Previous experience as a CNC machinist, CNC programmer, manufacturing technician, toolmaker, manufacturing engineer, machining supervisor, or similar role.

• Experience programming CNC mills and/or lathes.

• Experience with FANUC, Haas, or other commonly used CNC controls.

• Experience with CAD/CAM software such as Mastercam or similar platforms.

• Strong knowledge of blueprint reading, GD&T;, precision measurement, and inspection techniques.

• Prior teaching, technical training, apprenticeship, mentoring, or workforce-development experience.

• Industry-recognized machining or manufacturing credentials.

• Experience developing or delivering customized employer-based technical training.

• Experience troubleshooting CNC equipment, programs, tooling, and machining processes in a manufacturing environment.

Work Environment

This is a part-time, as-needed adjunct position. Training schedules vary based on employer and program needs and may include daytime, evening, or occasional weekend instruction. A significant portion of workforce training may occur during normal daytime business hours, particularly when training incumbent employees for local manufacturing partners. Instruction may take place at Ivy Tech Community College - Richmond or onsite at employer facilities. Local travel may be required. Course assignments will be based on the instructor's qualifications, CNC experience, technical expertise, availability, and employer training needs.

About the Opportunity

This position is well suited for experienced CNC machinists, CNC programmers, manufacturing technicians, toolmakers, manufacturing engineers, retirees, and other industry professionals interested in sharing their technical knowledge and experience. Applicants do not need previous college teaching experience to be considered. Professionals with strong hands-on industry experience and the ability to effectively demonstrate and explain machining concepts are encouraged to apply. Adjunct instructors can help Ivy Tech respond to the skilled manufacturing needs of area employers while remaining active in the industry on a flexible, part-time basis.

title: Senior Silicon Photonics Reliability Engineer
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

Why Intel Foundry

At Intel Foundry, you will help develop and enable next-generation silicon photonics technologies that power AI, cloud computing, networking, and high-speed communications. As part of a world-class engineering organization, you will work alongside leading scientists and engineers to solve complex reliability challenges, influence technology decisions, and bring innovative photonic technologies from research and development into high-volume manufacturing.

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the industry's most advanced Silicon Photonics programs and help deliver reliable, cutting-edge solutions to Intel Foundry customers worldwide.

About the Role

Intel's Silicon Photonics Quality & Reliability team is seeking a Senior Silicon Photonics Reliability Engineer to drive reliability strategy, qualification, and technology development for advanced photonic devices and Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs).

In this role, you will partner closely with technology development, process integration, design, manufacturing, and quality teams to assess, improve, and certify the reliability of silicon photonics technologies and products. You will play a key role in identifying reliability risks, developing qualification methodologies, resolving complex technical challenges, and ensuring successful transitions from technology development to high-volume manufacturing.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Assess and characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic reliability of photonic devices, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), lasers, and integrated optical products.
  • Develop reliability models and acceleration methodologies through Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, and reliability testing.
  • Drive reliability improvements through process, design, and material optimization efforts.
  • Develop and implement new reliability characterization techniques, screening methodologies, and quality controls.
  • Define reliability, qualification, and certification requirements for new silicon photonics technologies and products.
  • Lead failure analysis and root cause investigations using data-driven and model-based problem-solving techniques.
  • Evaluate reliability risks and provide recommendations to engineering and business stakeholders.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure quality and reliability requirements are integrated throughout the technology development lifecycle.
  • Support new technology introduction and successful transfer into high-volume manufacturing environments.
  • Analyze large data sets to identify trends, opportunities, and reliability risks using advanced statistical methods.
  • Present technical findings and recommendations to engineering leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, and executive management.
  • Contribute to reliability strategy, best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives across Intel Foundry's Silicon Photonics organization.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

  • Strong technical judgment and the ability to make sound decisions with incomplete information while appropriately balancing risk and business impact.
  • Ownership and accountability for driving complex technical initiatives from concept through implementation.
  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills with a structured, data-driven approach.
  • Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across engineering, manufacturing, quality, and business organizations.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for diverse audiences.
  • Capability to manage multiple priorities and execute effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a passion for developing innovative technologies.
  • Adaptability and resilience when navigating ambiguity and evolving business priorities.
  • A collaborative mindset and commitment to fostering an inclusive team environment.
  • Passion for quality, reliability, operational excellence, and customer success.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

  • See Intel Benefits for more details.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Note:

For information on Intel’s immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see

Intel U.S. Immigration Sponsorship Information

Minimum Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master's degree in Photonics/Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Semiconductor Engineering, or a related Stem degree with 4+ years of relevant experience. Or a PhD in in the same filed with 2+ years of relevant industry.
  • In addition, candidates should possess experience in one or more of the following areas:
    • 2+ years of silicon photonics, photonic devices, optical devices, or integrated photonics technology development.
    • 4+ years of semiconductor device characterization, validation, yield, reliability, or test engineering.
    • 4+ years with compound semiconductor processing and photonic device physics.
    • 4+ years of reliability engineering, qualification engineering, failure analysis, or technology development within semiconductor or photonics environments.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience:

  • PhD in Physics, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, or related engineering fields with 2+ years of experience in photonic devices.
  • Previous related work experience in a semiconductor foundry preferred.
  • Process certification/product qualification and reliability risk assessment, quality systems, and quality culture knowledge.
  • Semiconductor device physics and defect mechanism knowledge.
  • Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes, manufacturing process development, material characterization and development, and design validation.
  • Hands-on semiconductor wafer fabrication process and process integration challenges.
  • Reliability failure statistics, physics, failure mechanisms, and failure analysis methodologies.
  • Experience in of SPC/DOE principles, DOEs execution, and statistical analysis.
  • Data extraction and analysis skills (JMP/Crystal Ball/ILM/REL/PCS/SQL Scripting).
  • Knowledge of photonic datacom and telecom reliability qualification standards such as Telcordia GR-468, AEC-Q102.

title: Backend Technical Lead
description:
Company Description
Nine is Australia’s largest locally owned media company. Working at Nine, you’ll have access to a unique range of experiences and opportunities, helping drive the success of the country’s most trusted television, radio, digital and publishing brands.

Our content reaches almost every Australian - meaning what we do has real impact. We bring people together, celebrate the big moments, and capture the everyday ones.

Some of our most beloved brands have been part of Australian life for generations, and others - new on the scene - have already found their place firmly in our lives. We’re evolving and we need people like you to bring new ideas, innovate and make your mark.

Job Description

As Technical Lead you will lead the backend team responsible for the core streaming platform and APIs that power 9Now and Stan. This is a hands-on role for a technical expert passionate about building resilient, high-concurrency distributed systems while fostering the professional growth of a high-performing engineering team.


Day to day you will:


  • Lead by example by writing, reviewing, and deploying high-performance Go code.
  • Design and own the full lifecycle of cloud-based distributed systems and APIs.
  • Drive operational excellence through CI/CD, automated testing, and staged rollouts.
  • Line manage and mentor engineers to support their career growth and wellbeing.
  • Champion AI and automation to enhance system monitoring and infrastructure.
  • Collaborate with Product Managers to align technical roadmaps with business goals.
  • Resolve complex production issues by leading root-cause analysis and resolution.

What you’ll bring:


  • Prior experience leading engineering teams.
  • Deep technical expertise in developing and maintaining applications using Go.
  • Advanced cloud knowledge in AWS and distributed systems like microservices.
  • A DevOps mindset with proficiency in infrastructure-as-code and monitoring tools.
  • Strong security focus regarding application best practices and auditing.
  • A forward-thinking approach to leveraging AI for backend and operational efficiency.
  • Agile leadership skills to remove roadblocks and empower team autonomy.



Additional Information

How we work
At Nine, our flexible work options vary by role and team. Depending on the position, this may include flexible hours, hybrid work, or part-time arrangements. We welcome discussing your flexibility needs during the hiring process - just ask the Talent Acquisition team.

Our employee benefits include:

  • 18 weeks paid parental leave with no distinction between primary and secondary carers

  • Access to 'Employee Exclusives' program - a way of getting closer to our incredible brands, offering unique experiences, behind-the-scenes access, and awesome perks.

  • Digital newspaper subscription to our mastheads

  • Annual gift voucher for Stan subscription

  • More info at Nine Careers

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We're committed to a safe, respectful and inclusive Nine. From day one, you'll be encouraged to bring your whole self to work and will be supported to perform at your best.
We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disabilities, and of all ages, genders, nationalities, backgrounds and cultures as we recognise the importance and value of diverse perspectives. Should you require any adjustments to the recruitment process, please advise us when you apply.
Work rights: Please note to apply for this role you must already have the right to lawfully work and live in Australia.

title: AI Data & Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, we believe new insights have a way of becoming excellent products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there’s no telling what you could accomplish.

The people here at Apple don’t just build products — they build the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.

Manufacturing Systems and Infrastructure (MSI) team is an engineering organization under the Product Operations org. MSI is responsible for the design, development, and maintenance of systems tools, services, and applications required to efficiently run manufacturing operations at scale across global factory sites.

As an AI Data & Infrastructure Engineer with the MSI team, you will won the end to end design, build, and operation of scalable AI data systems that power enterprise GenAI and Agentic AI capabilities. Your work spans core platform services, data pipeline development and infrastructure provisioning, enabling manufacturing workflow automation through Agents and Agent skills.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ Experience designing and building scalable data platforms and distributed systems.
  • Strong programming skills in Python and SQL, with proficiency in Java or Scala preferred.
  • Experience with Airflow, Kubeflow, or MLflow to build and orchestrate scalable AI data pipelines.
  • Experience building scalable batch and streaming data pipelines using Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Airflow, and Ray, with proficiency in Pandas and modern data lake/lakehouse architectures (e.g., Iceberg, Delta Lake).
  • Experience using modern development tools, including AI-assisted coding tools, while applying sound engineering judgment to review, validate, and improve generated code.
  • Knowledge of RAG architectures, embedding generation, vector databases, and AI data preparation for LLMs and agentic AI.
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), Kubernetes, Docker, CI/CD, and Infrastructure as Code.
  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex user workflows, translate them into practical technical solutions, and collaborate across teams to deliver measurable outcomes.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into clear, business focused insights.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with or a strong understanding of Generative AI, LLMs, Agentic Systems, or RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) workflows.
  • Experience integrating LLMs into existing systems
  • Experience with API design, both for other engineers to use, but also for AI systems.
  • Experience working with manufacturing, operational, IoT, or industrial data platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives and mentor engineers.

title: PT Cake Decorator#415-2600 Ensign Hill Drive
description:
Cake Decorator
Position Objective: To assist customers in their shopping experience by providing them with beautifully decorated baked goods in the most efficient, friendly, and courteous manner possible.
Reporting Structure: This position formally reports to the Bakery Manager.
Status: This is a non-exempt position.
Knowledge
The following is a list of any certifications, formal education, or training requirements for this position.
Essential Knowledge
* A valid driver’s license is required for deliveries.
* A food handling permit must be obtained within the first 14 days of employment.
* Completion of ongoing training and development as listed on the Cosentino’s Learning Plan.
Non-Essential Knowledge
* A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred.
Skills
The following is a list of the basic skill requirements for this position.
Essential Job Functions
* Know and implement the Casentino Customer Service Standards.
* Consult with customers to determine the bakery items that best meet their needs and clearly document all orders to ensure follow through on service requests.
* Know your department products, procedures and policies so that you can accurately and courteously answer customer questions.
* Decorate various bakery items in a neat, creative and visually appealing manner.
* Merchandise cases to ensure fullness, freshness, and attractiveness of displays to promote sales.
* Effectively prepare, package and label product for sale.
* Rotate fresh product into cases, coolers, and freezers to prevent the sale or use of stale/outdated product.
* Be able to efficiently operate, clean and maintain cake decorating equipment, such as air brush, edible images, etc.
* Know, comply with, and encourage other team members to comply with all health regulations, sanitation guidelines and safety procedures for your department and your store.
* Able to operate, clean and maintain all equipment safely and competently.
* Meet or exceed productivity standards to produce desired team and individual results.
* Actively work to keep your work area and the department as a whole clean and safe for customers and coworkers.
* Resolve customer complaints in a professional manner and recognize when it is appropriate to involve a member of the store management team.
* Demonstrates the strong verbal and interpersonal skills necessary for positive customer and peer interactions.
* Demonstrates the basic math and reading skills required for the position.
Non-Essential Job Functions
* Promoting sales by suggesting additional products and offering samples.
* Efficiently restock bakery ingredients each day and notify the bakery manager of items that should be reordered.
* Quickly and neatly stock incoming bakery ingredients in their designated areas without damaging merchandise.
* Previous experience may be required in order to maintain the level of decorating skill and speed required of this position.
* Support your company by completing additional tasks identified by management, assisting other stores or departments as needed and gaining new skills when necessary.
Physical Abilities
The following physical movements could potentially be part of any scheduled shift and employees will be expected to perform these actions while on duty.
Essential Abilities
* Reaching overhead with both arms up to a maximum of 78 inches, twisting at the waist and lifting objects with both hands weighing up to 20 lbs.
* Pushing and pulling grocery items to the proper locations as needed, up to a peak force of 20lbs.
* Standing and walking for long periods of time on tile, asphalt, concrete or other hard surfaces.
* Occasionally lifting and carrying up to 35 lbs.
* Bending and squatting, at times all the way to floor level.
* Able to work in colder conditions of the grocery coolers and freezers.
Non-Essential Abilities
* Climbing a ladder, possibly up to 5ft.

title: Senior Product Manager, France Market Expansion
description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

As the Senior Product Manager for France Market Expansion at Clio, you will lead the vision, strategy, and roadmap execution of solutions that help Clio successfully expand into the French market. You will own the end to end product portfolio and customer experience for France, balancing global scale with local nuance. This role sits at the intersection of product execution and regional partnership, and it suits someone who thrives in complexity, builds for diverse users, and gets into the weeds.

Our market opportunity is rare in its scale and powered by a strong business model, first-rate investors and advisors, and a global product management team (if we do say so ourselves). Clio is growing rapidly, and Product Managers here grow their scope as we open new markets.

Speaking of Product at Clio, we have worked hard to develop an excellent product management culture with empowered PMs who carry real influence across the organization. Our team brings together seasoned professionals from a diverse set of product backgrounds. Clio invests heavily in developing Product Managers, growing leaders, and in the broader Product communities in which we operate.

What you'll work on:

As a Senior Product Manager, and in conjunction with your Development and Design counterparts (your triad), you will drive successful outputs and outcomes across Clio's portfolio in France.

End to End Portfolio Ownership:

  • You own Clio's product portfolio and customer experience in France end to end, from first touch through onboarding, daily practice management, billing, and support. Where a gap sits in a product another team owns, you own getting it closed.

  • You are accountable for the quality of Clio's customer experience in France as a whole, rather than for a single feature area. Your measure of success is whether a lawyer in France can run their practice on Clio without hitting a wall that a lawyer in North America would not hit.

  • You maintain a single, current view of what breaks today, what is missing, and what we have committed for France, and you make that view legible to leadership before leadership asks for it.

Product Leadership and Execution:

  • Working from the overarching strategy set by your Senior Director, Product Management, you will develop a roadmap in conjunction with your peers that moves our business forward, and evangelize it throughout the company.

  • You will own the delivery of features in the roadmap while also ensuring they deliver on the desired business outcome.

  • Drive product readiness for the French market, including localization, multi-lingual support, regulatory requirements, and market-specific workflows.

Speed and Iteration Toward a Clear Vision:

  • You set a clear vision for what Clio looks like in France, then ship toward it in weeks rather than quarters. We expect a first customer-visible change within your first 90 days.

  • You will make decisions with imperfect information, put something in front of customers, and correct from what you learn. We aim to validate with real customers before building at scale, however there are scenarios where a regulatory deadline sets the date. In those cases we will commit to the date and narrow the scope rather than move the date.

  • You parallelize. When a workstream can run alongside another, you run it alongside, and you say what serializing would cost in weeks when you choose to serialize.

Local Legal Market Understanding:

  • You understand how lawyers in France actually work: how French civil law shapes a firm's structure, how matters progress through the local courts, how the profession sets and regulates fees, what the Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres require of a practitioner, and where local practice diverges from common law practice.

  • You track the regulatory surface that touches our product, including French electronic invoicing under the Factur-X and PDP regime, TVA, and Conseil National des Barreaux professional rules, and you translate it into requirements our central teams can build against.

  • You build and maintain direct relationships with practitioners, bar associations, and local partners, and you serve as the company's source of truth on what the French legal profession needs.

System Design and Technical Fluency:

  • You can read and reason about how we built our platform: where our data models carry a country assumption, how the model represents currency, tax, payments, and locale, and what a change to one of those costs downstream.

  • You can hold a design discussion with engineering about cardinality, extensibility, and migration, and leave with a shared decision.

  • You can tell a problem that needs a local configuration from a problem that needs a platform capability, and you argue for the platform capability when it is the right answer.

AI Native Working Style:

  • You work AI-first by default. You use AI for customer research synthesis, competitive and regulatory analysis, requirements drafting, data querying, and prototyping, and you can show how it changed your throughput.

  • You build your own working systems. You are comfortable writing prompts, chaining tools, and standing up a lightweight agent or script to remove repetitive work from your week.

  • You bring judgment to it. You know which AI output needs verification against a primary source, particularly on regulatory and legal questions, and you verify it.

Influencing Central Teams:

  • Central teams build the platform that France depends on, and their leadership sets their goals, metrics, and roadmap without France in them. Your job is to quantify the case for France well enough that it wins a place on that roadmap.

  • You will build the business case in the currency that team's leadership measures it on, name the tradeoff you are asking them to make, and find the version of the ask that serves their goal alongside yours.

  • You escalate on a stated trigger rather than on frustration. When merit alone does not win the ask, you bring your Senior Director a clear recommendation and the cost of inaction.

Cross-Functional Partnership:

  • Partner closely with cross-functional leaders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Operations to support the French market launch and growth.

  • Manage stakeholder relationships across a matrixed organization with clarity and diplomacy.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in French and in English. Clio operates in English, so English fluency is a requirement of the role rather than a preference.

  • 4-5 years of experience in product management

  • Working knowledge of the French legal market, including French civil law, how local firms operate, and the regulatory requirements that apply to them

  • Proven track record of independently taking multiple products or features from ideation to launch in a SaaS environment

  • Experience owning a product area end to end, including outcomes that depended on teams outside your own

  • Demonstrated expertise in localization and multi-lingual product development. This is a core requirement for the role.

  • Experience building or managing multilingual applications or internationalization projects, and expanding products to other countries and languages

  • Technical fluency sufficient to reason about system design, data models, and platform tradeoffs with engineering

  • A demonstrated AI-native working style, with specific examples of how you use AI in your product practice

  • Evidence of winning roadmap commitments from teams that do not report to you and that carry no accountability for your outcome

  • Exceptional attention to detail, so that no requirement or specification slips through the product development cycle

  • Outstanding organizational skills, capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously without compromising quality or timelines

  • Experience using data to inform decisions without succumbing to analysis paralysis

  • Genuine ability to put yourself in our customers' shoes and operate from a place of empathy

  • Experience working across time zones and cultures, with a customer-first approach

  • An entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in ambiguity

  • At least 2 or 3 failures under your belt, the learnings of which you can bring to Clio

  • Ability to work in a highly collaborative team without ego

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Serious bonus points if you:

  • Have prior experience in legal tech, or a strong understanding of the legal services market, including familiarity with legal practice management software and the needs of legal professionals

  • Have worked directly with Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres or comparable professional bodies

  • Worked previously in a regulated industry or with multi-product ecosystems

  • Have shipped against a regulatory deadline in France or another EU market

  • Successfully launched products in global markets

  • Have a track record of breaking down objectives into initiatives and delivering to customers at scale

  • Have built internal tooling or agents to support your own product practice

  • Demonstrable experience self-serving answers, insights, and data from a variety of data analytics tools

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

  • Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits and dental coverage

  • Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.

  • Flexible time off policy

  • Pension contribution

  • Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

title: FPGA and Embedded SW Platform Team Lead
description:
TriEye is a deep tech company turning scientific breakthroughs into transformative sensing and electro optical capabilities. Built on cutting edge research in nanophotonics, semiconductors, and advanced optics, we develop proprietary technologies that push beyond the limits of conventional sensing, enabling systems to see, detect, understand, and act in ways that were previously impractical or impossible.

At the core of our technology is a new approach to SWIR sensing, enabled by our breakthrough CMOS based platform. But our innovation extends far beyond the sensor itself. By combining advanced semiconductor design, nanophotonics, proprietary laser and illumination technologies, computational sensing, and deep system level engineering, we create tightly integrated solutions with fundamentally new capabilities, not simply better performance or lower cost.

This full stack approach allows TriEye to rethink sensing from the physics up, translating advances at the material and device level into meaningful advantages at the system and application level.

We are looking for some exceptional talent to join our Design and Engineering team as a System Platform Team Lead

Your Day to Day

  • Lead a multidisciplinary team of embedded SW, FPGA/logic, verification and software engineers
  • Own the system-level architecture and execution of various SoC-based camera processing and control platforms including Xilinx MPSoC
  • Oversee development across ARM A53/R5, Linux, bare metal, FPGA logic, HLS, micro-controllers, host software, interfaces and system integration
  • Lead implementation and validation of image-processing algorithms developed by the algorithm team
  • Drive technical planning, design reviews, integration, debugging, risk management and execution
  • Stay hands-on through selected complex or quality-critical tasks to maintain deep system understanding
  • Coordinate closely with algorithms, electronics, sensor and system teams

Requirements

  • B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering or another relevant technical field
  • Senior-level experience in complex multidisciplinary systems, preferably in imaging or camera products
  • Experience leading engineering teams and driving execution
  • Strong system architecture background spanning embedded SW, FPGA/RTL, host-side software, HW/SW integration and interfaces
  • Experience with Xilinx Zynq / MPSoC or similar heterogeneous SoC platforms
  • Good understanding of Linux, bare-metal development, Verilog, Vivado/Vitis and FPGA development flows
  • Experience with Python and C++
  • Strong integration and debugging skills across hardware, FPGA and software
  • Experience with image/data processing pipelines and platforms such as PCs, Raspberry Pi or NVIDIA Jetson is an advantage
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
  • Fluent in English, both verbal and written

Why should you be a TriEyoneer?

  • Work at the edge of what’s possible

Turn scientific breakthroughs in sensing, photonics, and semiconductors into capabilities that were previously impractical or impossible.

  • Build what others can’t

Work across physics, hardware, software, and algorithms to build complex systems from first principles and take them all the way to real world deployment.

  • See your work make an impact

Build technology that moves beyond the lab into demanding real world applications across defense, robotics, industrial, and emerging markets.

  • Grow with exceptional people

Join a multidisciplinary team that values ownership, curiosity, technical excellence, and pushing boundaries together.

  • Enjoy the journey

Modern offices in Tel Aviv with easy access to public transport, plus a competitive benefits package including gym, parking, Cibus, generous vacation, and team events.

TriEye is an equal-opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

Job Details:

​General Notes

The College of Natural Sciences at the University of Texas at Austin strives to foster a work environment that enables all employees to contribute at the highest possible level to support the mission of the University. We are committed to being an inclusive community that celebrates the dignity of every individual, honors differences and lets each person know that they belong. What starts here really does change the world. For more information about the College of Natural Sciences, please visit: .

Must be eligible to work in the US on a full-time basis for any employer without sponsorship.

Purpose

The Senior Health Professions Coach advises UT Austin pre-health professions students on academic prerequisites and non-academic components of their preparation for application to professional school. This role also annually updates course and non-academic requirements by working with admissions representatives and leads event coordination for the office, advancing our core mission of fostering wellness, belonging, and success for all students.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as UT point of contact with health professions program representatives to verify course requirements annually, and school specific information to support student success and coordinate HP program representative presentations for coaches during roundtable meetings.

  • Provide coaching individually and in groups to pre-health professions students as they progress toward and complete application to professional schools. Use admissions data from Health Professions Schools to lead discussions with students.

  • Represent health professions programs and services in on-campus and off-campus organizations, meetings and conferences. Work collaboratively with members of the “Career Ecosystem” (Career Faculty Fellows, Academic Advisors, Experiential Learning Advisors, Career Coaches, other pre-Health Professions Coaches, and administrative staff). Serve as HPO liaison to tc3, student organizations and as the chapter advisor for AED. This will include evening events for student organizations.

  • Stay current on admissions requirements across these disciplines: Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary, Pharmacy, Optometry, Physician Assistant, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Cardio Perfusion, Orthotics and Prosthetics, Anesthesiology Assistant, and Podiatry through research of in-state and out-of-state professional schools.

  • Plan and coordinate workshops, seminars, and skill building events around hp career topics for students in person and through livestream. Prepare recorded versions of workshops and presentations. Teach and present to internal and external groups ranging in size from 25 to over 500.

  • Develop, select, and utilize effective pre-Health Professions materials for students pursuing a health professions career. Disseminate materials and information about professional school preparation and expectations to students, staff, and faculty as part of the “Career Ecosystem”.

  • Coordinate the HP Fair annually each spring with support from the CNS Events team. Work with professional schools and all vendors involved with the fair. Coordinate additional events as needed.

  • Teach spring seminar course, BIO 102C, for the Biology Scholars Program.

  • Serve as the HPO email triage lead.

  • Other duties as assigned, including supporting special projects, transition needs, and staffing CNS events.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree and four years of experience in academic advising, career services, or pre-health professions advising. Demonstrated project management abilities, interpersonal skills, professional demeanor and excellence in oral and written communication. Experience planning large-scale events. Experience teaching or presenting in classroom settings. Demonstrated ability to work in a collaborative team environment. Must be able to occasionally travel, including overnight travel.

Proficiency in MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

More experience than above. Experience as a health professions advisor in a university environment. Experience working with health professional and graduate schools.

Job Description:

Hitachi Rail is looking for an enthusiastic self-motivated IS/IT/Cyber Systems Engineer who thrives in a fast-paced environment. The successful candidate is comfortable performing a wide range of tasks from administrative to strategic. The position is based in Sydney, Australia.

The IS/IT/Cyber Systems Engineer is responsible for the design, specification, configuration, deployment, and support of project IT and cyber infrastructure across the Sydney Metro West (SMW) project and future programmes, including Parramatta Light Rail Stage 2. The role ensures that system and product inputs are translated into practical, scalable, and maintainable IT solutions, covering data centre infrastructure, virtualisation platforms, storage, and end-user systems across OCC, BOCC, stations, and associated facilities.

The SMW project includes a distributed IT environment requiring consistent design and implementation across multiple locations. This includes centralised data centre environments, station-based systems, and operational end-user platforms. A dedicated engineering role is required to ensure that IT infrastructure is consistently defined, procured, configured, and deployed in alignment with system requirements and internal product standards, providing continuity across design, delivery, and early operations.

Key accountabilities:

The IS/IT/Cyber Systems Engineer is responsible for the end-to-end implementation of IT infrastructure, including:

  • Translating product line and system engineering inputs into IT system designs

  • Defining equipment specifications for procurement, including servers, storage, and end-user devices

  • Designing virtualisation environments, including Proxmox clusters across OCC, BOCC, and witness sites, as well as standalone station clusters

  • Configuring and deploying compute, storage, and virtual platforms

  • Designing, developing, and implement cyber solutions for the project

  • Supporting procurement activities, including technical evaluation of equipment

  • Supporting integration, testing, and commissioning of IT/Cyber systems

  • Providing technical support during deployment and early operations

  • Defining and configuring workstations, monitors, video walls, handheld devices, and associated infrastructure

  • Maintaining design consistency and configuration control across all system

Required skills and knowledge:

  • Experience in IT systems or infrastructure engineering within complex environments

  • Strong knowledge of virtualisation platforms, clustering, and distributed systems

  • Knowledge of Cyber technologies for the OT environment

  • Experience in server, storage, and end-user system deployment

  • Ability to support system configuration, testing, and commissioning

  • Understanding of resilient and scalable IT architecture principles

  • Experience producing technical documentation and supporting procurement

  • Relevant qualifications in Information Technology, Systems Engineering, or similar

At Hitachi Rail, we know that a diverse business is a sustainable business. Working collaboratively with a range of internal networks, we’re continuously improving our policies and products. From accessible, sustainable design to achieving a better gender balance. We base these efforts on our core values: Harmony, Sincerity, and Pioneering spirit. And by aligning with these, we’re able to create a workplace where people not only feel comfortable but are given opportunities to thrive. We’re especially keen to hear from women and people of all genders considering a career in engineering, cybersecurity, and rail technology.

What we offer:

  • Ongoing professional development and training.
